OPPORTUNITY.title: Augrael Shares Library Knowledge
OPPORTUNITY.description: Augrael, the ghoulish morlock, appears peacefully reading. 'Oh! Visitors! I know this library well. Would you like directions? I only eat undead flesh, I promise.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 15 Diplomacy to befriend him
OPPORTUNITY.success: He provides detailed Floor 3 library map and warns about Nhakazarin's temple. PLUS gain 'Prepared' token. Next time you'd add dice to jar, spend token to add 1 fewer die (min 0). Information AND efficiency!
OPPORTUNITY.failure: He's hurt by your rejection and returns to his books.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. Augrael is unique NPC - tranquil, rejected by both morlocks and ghouls. Great recurring character. BONUS: Success grants Prepared token for future time savings. Track on character sheets.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Information + Prepared token (time savings)

OPPORTUNITY.title: Mitflit Squabble Over Shiny
OPPORTUNITY.description: Two mitflits fight over a shiny button, squeaking loudly, completely oblivious to you.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 14 Stealth to sneak past, OR DC 16 Intimidation to scare them
OPPORTUNITY.success: Slip past unnoticed, or mitflits flee dropping 2d6 sp.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: They screech an alarm before fleeing.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. Mitflits are cowardly but loud.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Avoid encounter or small treasure

OPPORTUNITY.title: Gladiator's Hidden Cache
OPPORTUNITY.description: Behind loose arena stone, a cache left by a dead gladiator. Note: 'For whoever survives this hell.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 16 Perception to find, DC 17 Athletics to retrieve from high alcove
OPPORTUNITY.success: Find +1 striking weapon, healing potion (moderate), 50gp. Note gives inspiration: +1 attack in arena for 1 hour.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Can't reach it, or cache already looted.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 5. Gladiators hid escape supplies. Inspiration applies to arena encounters.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Combat gear and morale

OPPORTUNITY.title: Bog Mummy Burial Mound
OPPORTUNITY.description: Ancient burial mound where Children of Belcorra inter their dead. Grave goods visible but disturbing feels wrong.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 17 Religion to perform proper rites, DC 18 Thievery to take items without desecration
OPPORTUNITY.success: Respectfully take: 100gp ancient coins, +1 resilient armor. No curse. Or perform rites: +1 saves vs undead 24 hours.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Desecrate mound. Curse: -1 all saves until atone, or awaken bog mummy guardian.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. Moral choice: respect dead or take treasure? Curse is real if desecrated.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Treasure or blessing vs undead

OPPORTUNITY.title: Deep Gnome Memorial
OPPORTUNITY.description: A touching memorial to the deep gnomes before they became bog mummies. Names, trinkets, memories.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 16 Society to understand their history, DC 18 Diplomacy to honor their memory
OPPORTUNITY.success: Understand tragedy of Children of Belcorra. Gain their blessing: +2 to Diplomacy with undead on this floor.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Disturb memorial - bog mummies sense disrespect and hunt you.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. Tragic lore. Deep gnomes were enthralled, not evil. Respect earns their aid.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Lore and undead diplomacy

OPPORTUNITY.title: Darklands Faction Stash
OPPORTUNITY.description: Hidden supply cache belonging to a Darklands faction (drow, urdefhan, or caligni). Trapped but full.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 19 Thievery to disarm trap, DC 18 Society to identify which faction
OPPORTUNITY.success: Safely loot: 3 healing potions, 75gp, faction gear. Knowing faction helps avoid/negotiate (+2 Diplomacy).
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Trap triggers: 3d6 damage, alerts nearby faction members, or can't identify faction.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. Roll faction: 1-2 drow, 3-4 urdefhan, 5-6 caligni. Faction hostile if discover theft.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Supplies and faction knowledge

OPPORTUNITY.title: Faction Territory Markers
OPPORTUNITY.description: Crude territorial markers showing faction boundaries. Symbols, warnings, and threat displays.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 17 Survival to read markers, DC 18 Society to understand faction politics
OPPORTUNITY.success: Learn safe paths through territories, or understand faction alliances/enemies (+2 to navigate floor).
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Misread markers - accidentally enter hostile territory.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. Factions are territorial. Understanding politics allows safe passage or exploitation.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Safe navigation

OPPORTUNITY.title: Stone Scale Totem in the Puddle
OPPORTUNITY.description: Half-sunk in a puddle of swamp water lies a kobold clan totem: a carved post of black bog-oak topped with a lizard skull, one eye socket still holding a polished red stone. Rows of tiny notches run down the post - and the last name in the column has been gouged out with a knife.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 15 Thievery or Crafting to pry the stone out without cracking it (10 minutes). DC 15 Society to read the Draconic notches.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You free a bloodstone eye (6 gp). The notches are a list of Stone Scale chieftains; the gouged-out last name and the knife marks tell you the clan ended in a coup, not an invasion.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The stone cracks as it comes loose (2 gp). The notches are too waterlogged to read.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. The Stone Scale kobolds who squatted in the ruins destroyed themselves in a violent coup; their spirits haunt the old dining hall (A7). If the party later faces the Stone Scale Spirits haunt, a hero who read the notches knows the haunt is about the coup and gets +2 circumstance to the Religion or Intimidation check to end it.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Bloodstone (6 gp); lore that explains the Stone Scale Spirits haunt

OPPORTUNITY.title: MAJIK PIXY MUD
OPPORTUNITY.description: A cracked clay pot sits in a nook at knee height, its lid weighed down with a rock. Scratched into the side in crude Undercommon: MAJIK PIXY MUD. It smells exactly like what it is - mitflit dung - but something glints near the bottom.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Reach in and dig: DC 15 Fortitude save or sickened 1 for 10 minutes. DC 15 Nature to realize you can tip it out with a stick instead and skip the save.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Buried in the muck: two peridot beads (2 gp each) and a tarnished silver ring (5 gp). One of the Mud Lickers hid its 'candy' here to keep it from the others.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You find the beads but the ring slips down a crack in the floor.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. The Mud Lickers use 'magic pixie mud' as a prank on intruders (A1) - this pot is the source. If a mitflit sees the party take the beads it shrieks 'THIEF!' and runs to warn Boss Skrawng (A10).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 9 gp in peridot beads and a silver ring

OPPORTUNITY.title: Crook's Nook Fish-Cake Wrapper
OPPORTUNITY.description: On a mossy step lies a waxed paper wrapper with smoked-salmon crumbs still stuck to it, and beside it a lockpick roll whose leather flap is stamped with a small carved bird in flight. Muddy boot prints lead toward the water.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 15 Society to recognize the fish cakes as Crook's Nook fare; DC 16 Society to recognize the flying bird as the mark of the Osprey Club, Otari's thieves' guild.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You recover a Thieves' Toolkit (3 gp) and learn that Osprey Club thieves came through here recently, heading for the cavern under the island.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You take the lockpicks, but don't connect them to anyone in particular.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. Four Osprey Club thieves came looking for treasure in the cavern under the island (B19); the river drake Fresnel Kes cut off their escape and the morlocks captured them - one is dead, three are held in B24. Yinyasmera at Crook's Nook pays 50 gp for news of them. Showing her this lockpick roll proves the party found their trail.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Thieves' Toolkit; a lead on Yinyasmera's missing thieves (50 gp side quest)

OPPORTUNITY.title: Antlered Clasp in the Scorch Marks
OPPORTUNITY.description: This wall is scarred black where some spell detonated centuries ago, and the rubble beneath has fused into glassy lumps. Something small and silver catches your light inside one of them: a cloak clasp shaped like a pair of antlers, half melted.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 15 Perception to spot it; DC 15 Athletics or Crafting to crack it free of the slag (10 minutes). DC 15 Religion identifies the antlers as the symbol of Erastil.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You free the clasp. It belonged to a cleric of Erastil who fought here - and the only cleric of Erastil in the Roseguard was Aesephna Menhemes, Otari's founder.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The clasp snaps in half as you pry it loose. It's still recognizable, but worth only scrap silver (2 gp).
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. The Roseguard confronted Belcorra in A4 and the fight ran through the keep, collapsing parts of it. Mayor Oseph Menhemes is Aesephna's descendant; returning the clasp earns 25 gp and makes him well disposed toward the party when they later need his Hunter's Brooch for the Roseguard icons.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Silver clasp (8 gp as scrap, or 25 gp from Mayor Oseph Menhemes)

OPPORTUNITY.title: Maggot Pupae in the Carcass
OPPORTUNITY.description: A dead heron lies in the reeds, crawling with something. Three fist-sized brown husks are packed into its body cavity, twitching. A crude mud drawing on the wall beside it shows a mitflit riding a fly the size of a pony.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 15 Nature to recognize giant maggot pupae a week or two from hatching. Crushing them all quietly takes DC 15 Athletics (10 minutes).
OPPORTUNITY.success: You destroy three future giant flies - three fewer 'war steeds' for Boss Skrawng's planned raid on Otari.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: One pupa splits as you work and a slick, half-formed fly flops out, buzzing loudly. You kill it, but the noise carries.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. Boss Skrawng plans to breed giant flies as cavalry and conquer Otari (A4-A6, A10). On a failure, roll a DC 10 flat check; on a success 1d2 Mitflits come to see what the buzzing was.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Weakens Boss Skrawng's army; one fewer Giant Maggot in the next Floor 1 combat that includes maggots

OPPORTUNITY.title: The Treasure Hunter Who Took the Silver
OPPORTUNITY.description: A skeleton lies face-down in the mud below a broken wall, a rusted chisel still in its fist. A rotted satchel strap is caught on its ribs, and through a tear you can see dull silver gleaming - thin curls of it, like shavings off a carving.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Haul the satchel out of the sucking mud: DC 15 Athletics (10 minutes). DC 18 Arcana or Occultism to recognize the curls as rune-silver gouged out of a teleportation circle.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You recover 6 gp of rune-silver and the chisel. Studying the silver, you realize someone stripped a teleportation circle here centuries ago - which destroys such circles permanently.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The satchel tears and the silver scatters into the muck; you salvage 2 gp of it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. This is the fortune hunter who gouged the silver out of the hidden circle in A4 and destroyed it forever. He foreshadows the portal chambers deeper down (B17 and others), which are intact and can be reawakened with the awaken portal ritual. A hero who made the Arcana check recognizes the network's rune pattern on sight later.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 6 gp of rune-silver; lore about Belcorra's teleportation circles

OPPORTUNITY.title: Skrawng's Price List
OPPORTUNITY.description: Scratched into a beam at mitflit height is a row of pictograms: a stick-figure mitflit holding a coin, then a crude map, then a figure with a crown nodding. Under the coin someone has scratched two little circles.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 15 Society to puzzle out the Mud Licker pictograms (or automatic for anyone who reads Undercommon).
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a price list: two gold coins buys a map from the boss. Boss Skrawng can be bribed.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The drawings stay gibberish.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. Canon: Skrawng becomes helpful for a bribe of at least 2 gp plus something to write with. His Level 1 map omits A12-A13, A19-A23, A25 and all secret doors; his Level 2 map shows only the mitflits' old areas (B8-B14, B16-B19) with a warning about the 'swamp dragon' in B19.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Any bribe of 2 gp or more automatically makes Boss Skrawng helpful; he trades a crude map of Level 1 and part of Level 2

OPPORTUNITY.title: Lighthouse Paint That Never Dried
OPPORTUNITY.description: At the foot of the lighthouse's smooth gray wall stands a rusted paint pot, its brush fused to the rim. Inside, the gray paint is still wet - after five hundred years. A faint blue shimmer moves across its surface when the lighthouse glows overhead.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 15 Arcana or Occultism to understand what you're looking at.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The paint is part of the Gauntlight itself: the same magic that keeps the lighthouse undamaged keeps this pot fresh. You seal some into a vial - Wrin Sivinxi would pay for it.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You can't work out why the paint is wet. It's still a curiosity.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 1. Gauntlight is protected from damage by its own magic, and that effect has bled into the ruins and slowed their decay. Wrin is the only person in Otari who can see the glow from town; if she gets the paint she can study it and tells the party the lighthouse is drawing power from somewhere far below.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Vial of Gauntlight paint (15 gp to Wrin Sivinxi, 3 gp to anyone else)

OPPORTUNITY.title: Clockwork Arm in the Hallway
OPPORTUNITY.description: A brass arm the length of a man lies in the corridor, ripped from something larger. Its fingers are still curled around a feather duster. Two of its joints use cut gemstones as bearings, and a plate on the shoulder is engraved: PROPERTY OF THE MAJORDOMO.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 16 Crafting to pop the gemstone bearings out without cracking them (10 minutes).
OPPORTUNITY.success: You recover two gemstone bearings (5 gp each).
OPPORTUNITY.failure: One bearing cracks; you salvage the other (5 gp).
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 2. Clockwork assistants once maintained this level; the morlocks scavenge them for parts (B9, B26). Engineers rebuilding ballistae in B22 dragged this arm off and dropped it. A hero who handles the arm recognizes the same gear work on any clockwork assistant they find later and gets +2 circumstance to Crafting to salvage it.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 10 gp in gemstone bearings

OPPORTUNITY.title: Where the Licked-Clean Stripe Ends
OPPORTUNITY.description: Down the middle of a filthy corridor runs a stripe of stone so clean it gleams - about a tongue's width, wet in places. It ends abruptly at a pile of grime. A tiny silver bell lies half buried in the muck where the cleaning stopped.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 16 Survival or Perception to read the trail: which way the cleaner came from and how fresh it is.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You pocket the bell (8 gp) and work out the cleaner's route and timing. Gain 1 Prepared token.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You get the bell, but can't tell where the cleaner went - or when it's coming back.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 2. Zolazarin the zebub is contractually Belcorra's janitor: 18 hours a day in his painted room (B27) and 6 hours buzzing through the level cleaning - at least 3 of them with his tongue. Knowing his route lets the party avoid him. Prepared token: next time the party would add dice to the jar, add 1 fewer (minimum 0).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Silver servant's bell (8 gp); 1 Prepared token on a success

OPPORTUNITY.title: The Servant's Loose Brick
OPPORTUNITY.description: In a ruined servant's alcove, one brick sits slightly proud of the wall. Scratched beside it in tiny marks: a tally of days, hundreds of them, in neat groups of five.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 16 Perception to notice which brick is loose. DC 16 Thievery to work it out without the mortar crumbling and jamming it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Behind it is a tin box holding a jade shard (15 gp) and a folded note.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The brick jams halfway. You can reach the note but not the box.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 2. The note: 'If the Mistress ever falls, go UP, not down. The library people are always hungry.' When Belcorra died, many of her servants fled, some hid, and the rest became food for the cannibal librarians on Level 3. Borbo hid his own stash behind a loose brick in B4 - the servants all did this.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Jade shard (15 gp) and a servant's note

OPPORTUNITY.title: Drag Marks and an Osprey Pin
OPPORTUNITY.description: Four parallel scrapes run through the mud on the floor - something heavy was dragged this way, struggling. Caught in a crack where the marks swerve is a pin shaped like a diving bird, and beside it a cloth bundle with a potion vial inside.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 16 Survival to follow the drag marks; DC 16 Society to recognize the bird as the Osprey Club, Otari's thieves' guild.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You recover a Healing Potion (Lesser) and the pin, and the marks show where prisoners are being taken.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You find the potion and pin, but lose the trail in a stretch of rubble.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 2. The morlocks captured four Crook's Nook thieves; one died as a sacrifice in B14, and three (Goru Vetas, Shad Nander, Zilli) are held in B24 behind a door barricaded from B22. Their gear is in B23. Yinyasmera pays 50 gp for their rescue; the pin proves the party found them.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Healing Potion (Lesser); proof for Yinyasmera's missing-thieves reward

OPPORTUNITY.title: Shed Scale with Acid Burns
OPPORTUNITY.description: A blue-green scale the size of your palm lies in the mud near a seep of swamp water. Its edges are pitted and smoking faintly, as if something caustic dripped on it.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 18 Arcana or Nature to identify the creature it came from.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a river drake scale - and the burns are its own caustic mucus. You also recall river drakes hunt at night, flee when badly hurt, and avoid brown mold.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Some kind of drake. That's all you can tell.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 2. Fresnel Kes, a female river drake, has lived in the flooded cavern (B19) for nearly two years, hunting only in the Fogfen so Otari doesn't know she exists. She flees below 10 HP and refuses to follow prey into the brown mold on the beach (B20) - a hero who made the check knows the mold is a safe refuge from her.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Drake scale (10 gp to an Otari alchemist); +2 circumstance to Recall Knowledge about the river drake

OPPORTUNITY.title: Tribute Pouch on a Sleeping Morlock
OPPORTUNITY.description: A morlock scavenger is curled up asleep in a corner, snoring, arms wrapped around a lumpy pouch. Through the open top you can see a dark red stone and the glint of a small copper locket.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 16 Thievery to lift the pouch without waking it, or DC 16 Stealth to slip past.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You take the pouch: a bloodstone (10 gp) meant as tribute for the Ghost Queen, and a copper locket holding a tiny portrait of an Otari couple.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: It wakes with a startled howl. Roll initiative - it fights until hurt, then runs to warn the others.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 2. The morlocks leave offerings at the bone statue in their Ghost Queen shrine (B14) but fear it too much to visit often. The locket was taken from a grave in Otari's cemetery after the Deadtide. Returning it earns 5 gp and a free meal from the grateful family.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Bloodstone (10 gp); a locket an Otari family will want back

key_abilities: Flees to warn King Graulgust when hurt

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Ribbon of Green Light
OPPORTUNITY.description: A thread of eerie green light slides out from under a door, forms letters on the far wall - I WAS OTARI. SAVE ME FROM BELOW. - then peels off the stone and slithers away along the floor like a serpent.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Follow it before it fades: it moves at 20 feet and lasts only a few minutes. DC 16 Perception to keep it in sight around corners.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It leads you to a stair whose top riser has a hidden catch. The ribbon slips under the secret door and fades - you've found a way down to Level 3.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You lose it in the dark. It will appear again tomorrow.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 2. Otari Ilvashi's unquiet spirit left echoes in the three places he hid during his last days (B28, C3, D16). The ribbon appears once per day and leads from B28 to the secret door at B32 (DC 18 Perception; push the top riser), which opens onto stairs to C10. The next message is in C3.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Discover a secret stair down to Level 3; first clue on Otari Ilvashi's trail

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Spool of Trip Cord
OPPORTUNITY.description: Wedged behind a pipe is a spool of thin, greasy cord, nearly invisible in dim light. Someone has tied knots in it at regular intervals - about one foot apart.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 16 Crafting or Society to work out what the knots are for.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's the morlocks' trap cord: the knots mark the one-foot height they string their tripwires at. From now on you know exactly where to look.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Just a spool of cord - still useful as rope.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 2. The morlocks dismantled the majordomo's furniture to build spike launchers triggered by near-invisible lines 1 foot off the floor (B10). On a success, the party automatically notices morlock tripwires on this floor; morlocks themselves move through freely because they know the lines.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 50 feet of fine cord (as rope); auto-spot morlock tripwires on Floor 2 on a success

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Librarian's Commonplace Book
OPPORTUNITY.description: A reading table sits half buried under stacks of identical gray folios, and a thread of pale blue robe-cloth is snagged on one corner. Under the top layer is a small book bound in red calfskin, its clasp worn smooth by a thumb - a librarian's personal commonplace book, kept before and after she became a ghoul.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Searching the stacks thoroughly: DC 18 Perception to spot it among the folios. DC 18 Society to recognize it as a personal journal worth more than a library volume.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You find it. Morlibint at Odd Stories will pay well for a first-hand account from inside Belcorra's library - and one entry stops you cold.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The stacks all blur together. You come away with nothing but dust.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 3. The entry, in a hand that grows shakier line by line: 'Day 1,206 after the Mistress fell. The stores are gone. Nhakazarin says hunger is a form of devotion. I wrote it down so I would not be the one who said it.' The Cult of the Canker turned to cannibalism rather than risk alerting the Roseguard by going to the surface, and ghoul fever followed. Counts toward Morlibint's 12-Bulk side quest as 1 Bulk.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Red calfskin commonplace book (20 gp to Morlibint, who normally pays 5 gp per Bulk)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Canker Effigy
OPPORTUNITY.description: A tiny figure lies on the floor where someone dropped it: a stick-man of finger bones, lashed together with knotted gray hair. A scrap of pale blue robe is tied around its waist like a sash.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 18 Religion to understand what it is.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a Canker Cult effigy - each ghoul in the cult has exactly one at the shrine, made from its own hair. This one belongs to whichever ghoul wears the torn robe. Its tiny eyes are gold wire (4 gp).
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A grisly trinket. The gold wire is worth 4 gp.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 3. Two dozen effigies of small bones and knotted hair surround the Canker Shrine (C24), one for each cult ghoul. If the party meets the ghoul in the torn robe (GM's choice), showing it the effigy makes it frightened 1, and the party gets +2 circumstance to Intimidation against it.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Gold wire (4 gp); leverage over one cult ghoul

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Book from Morlibint's List
OPPORTUNITY.description: A toppled book cart has spilled a dozen volumes across the floor. One spine reads 'Seven Sieges of the Starstone, Vol. II' - and its margins are crammed with notes in a sharp, elegant hand.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 18 Society to recognize it as one of the rare titles Morlibint is hunting, and to read the margin notes.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's on the list. The notes catalogue how each past siege of Absalom failed - written by someone planning a new one.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: It's an old history book. You take it anyway.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 3. The margin notes are Belcorra's. Her siege research is concentrated in the Siege Castle History room (C30), guarded by a wood golem carved in her likeness. Any hero who read the notes gets +2 circumstance to Society checks about Belcorra's plans for Absalom.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Rare title worth 1 Bulk plus a 10 gp bonus from Morlibint; lore about Belcorra's planned attack

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Spare Blue Robe
OPPORTUNITY.description: A long robe of faded pale blue hangs from a hook beside a doorway, the hem stiff with old blood. It's the same robe every ghoul librarian on this level wears.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Put it on: DC 18 Deception to carry yourself like one of the cult, the next time it matters.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Disguised in the robe, the next group of cult ghouls you meet on Floor 3 stops to ask if you've come to donate flesh for the canker, instead of attacking on sight.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The robe fits badly and smells worse. Ghouls see through it at once.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 3. The four ghouls in C11 wear long pale blue robes, lick their lips at the party, and ask whether they're here to donate flesh for the canker. A hero 'foolish enough to agree' must cut off a finger, toe or ear, which the ghoul carries to C34. The disguise buys one conversation, not safety.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: One cult ghoul encounter opens with a parley instead of an attack

OPPORTUNITY.title: Wishing Coins in the Drain
OPPORTUNITY.description: A rusted grate in the floor drains water away down a long pipe. Something glints between the bars: coins, dozens of them, caught on a lip just below the grate.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Lift the grate: DC 18 Athletics (10 minutes).
OPPORTUNITY.success: You fish out 30 silver pieces and a little tin token stamped with a lighthouse and the words LET ME GO HOME.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The grate won't budge. You can see the coins, but not reach them.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 3. Superstitious servants once tossed coins down toward the reservoir pool (C40) as wishes. A gibbering mouther lives in that cavern now; the drain carries sound both ways, so a failed check that clangs the grate loudly has a 1-in-4 chance of drawing its gibbering up the pipe (DC 18 Will vs. confused for 1 round).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 30 sp and a servant's wishing token

OPPORTUNITY.title: An Iridescent Quill
OPPORTUNITY.description: A quill lies on the floor, its feather shimmering through every color like oil on water. It's still wet with ink. A book lies open nearby on a page of sacrifice diagrams, and someone has scrawled SO FUNNY!! beside them in a bright, looping hand.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 18 Arcana or Occultism to identify the magic in the quill and who it belongs to.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a fey quill that never needs dipping. Its owner is a lurker in light - a mischievous, dangerous fey that has been reading in the library.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A pretty quill. You have no idea whose it is.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 3. Shimmerin, a lurker in light, slipped into Belcorra's Reading Room (C27) out of curiosity and is annotating Pathways of the Worm. Below 20 HP they dimension door away and plot revenge, likely allying with the ghouls in C33. Dimming a room's light stops their escape. Returning the quill makes Shimmerin Indifferent instead of hostile.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Fey quill (25 gp to Wrin Sivinxi); warning about the lurker in light

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Vision of the Last Supper
OPPORTUNITY.description: The corridor flickers. For a heartbeat it's 500 years ago: lamps lit, carpets new, a frightened servant girl hurrying past with a silver gravy boat clutched to her chest. She glances back toward the sound of choking from the dining room, presses a panel in the wall, shoves the gravy boat inside, and runs. Then the vision is gone.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 19 Perception to find the panel she pressed (10 minutes). DC 19 Society to work out what you saw.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The panel swings open. Inside is the silver gravy boat (25 gp), tarnished black. You understand the vision: you just watched Belcorra's guests being poisoned.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You can't find the panel - the vision didn't show quite where her hand went.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 4. Spectral visions of rooms as they were 500 years ago are a feature of this level. When the Roseguard attacked, Belcorra was dining (D1) with envoys from an Absalom thieves' guild she was courting. She excused herself, told them to finish their meal, and magically ordered her chef to poison the guests, murder the servants and kill himself. The guests' corpses now host corpselights.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Silver gravy boat (25 gp); lore about Belcorra's last dinner

OPPORTUNITY.title: Leech-Slime Footprints
OPPORTUNITY.description: A trail of wet, glistening prints runs down the hall - roughly humanoid, but each one smeared at the edges as if the foot were made of many small things squirming. A fat leech lies dying beside the trail, and next to it a dropped page covered in architectural lines.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 19 Crafting or Society to read the drawing. DC 19 Occultism to understand what made the footprints.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The page is a fragment of a blueprint of the upper levels showing one secret door you haven't found. The footprints belong to a worm-that-walks: a creature made of thousands of leeches.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Smudged lines and squirming prints. You can't make sense of either.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 4. Volluk Azrinae became a worm-that-walks by feeding himself to a vat of leeches. His desk in the Lounge (D8) holds full blueprints of the top three levels, including every secret door. He carries the lantern of empty light on trips aboveground - which unknowingly spawned Otari's rumors of a lantern-carrying stranger.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Map fragment revealing one secret door on Levels 1-3 (GM's choice); warning about Volluk

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Bottle That Rolled Away
OPPORTUNITY.description: A dust-furred wine bottle lies in the middle of the hallway, as if it rolled here on its own. The wax seal is intact. The faded label reads 'Haruvex Reserve, 4228 - for the Guild.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 19 Society to judge whether this vintage survived five centuries.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It did. This is a collector's bottle, magically kept from turning.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You can't tell whether it's priceless or vinegar.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 4. The wine cellar (D4) holds three valuable bottles among the spoiled ones (DC 18 Society). This one is a fourth that an ephemeral spirit moved - the spirits on this level tidy, close doors and move things around. Drinking it is harmless and delicious.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Valuable vintage (20 gp)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Wooden Rockfish Pin
OPPORTUNITY.description: Something small and carved lies in the dust by the wall: a wooden pin shaped like a grumpy fish, its paint worn by years of thumbs. A faint dwarven rune is carved on the back. Drag marks lead away down the corridor.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 19 Society (DC 15 for anyone who's drunk at the Rowdy Rockfish) to recognize it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's the Rowdy Rockfish's mascot - the kind of pin its staff wear. Lasda Venkervale, the dwarf barkeep who disappeared from Otari over a year ago, was brought this way.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A carved fish. Somebody's keepsake.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 4. Volluk abducted Lasda on one of his early walks from the Rockfish to the graveyard, held him for months in the torture chamber (D11), and then made him the living anchor of the Gauntlight in D9. Freeing him ends the necromantic ribbons in B35, C15 and D9. His mother Brelda gives the party her rockfish-emblazoned minor sturdy shield when he's returned; the pin earns her gratitude now.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Proof that Lasda is alive below; Brelda Venkervale gives the party free room and board for a week and 10 gp

OPPORTUNITY.title: The Guildmaster Who Almost Got Away
OPPORTUNITY.description: A skeleton in rotted velvet finery slumps against the wall far from any dining room, one hand still clawing at its throat. It made it a long way before the poison caught up with it. A heavy signet ring hangs loose on one finger bone.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 19 Religion or Perception to check whether a corpselight is nesting inside it before you touch it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The skeleton is empty. The ring bears the sigil of an Absalom thieves' guild that died out centuries ago.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: As your hand touches the ring, green light kindles in the ribcage. Roll initiative.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 4. One of the Absalom thieves'-guild envoys Belcorra poisoned at her last dinner (D1). Corpselights leap to new corpses whenever their host is destroyed, so any skeleton on this level might be occupied. Yinyasmera collects guild history and pays a premium.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Extinct-guild signet ring (30 gp, or 40 gp from Yinyasmera at Crook's Nook)

key_abilities: Jumps to a new corpse when its host is destroyed

OPPORTUNITY.title: Shed Spines and Gnawed Bones
OPPORTUNITY.description: Long chitinous spines lie scattered around a heap of picked-clean bones. Some are as long as your forearm and still oozing at the root. Whatever shed them is big, many-legged, and starving.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 19 Nature or Occultism to identify the creature.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Scalathrax: spider-like aberrations - the same kind of creature the Gauntlight teleported into Otari during the Deadtide. These ones are kept hungry on purpose.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Some kind of aberration. Big and hungry.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 4. Two poorly fed scalathrax remain in their pen (D10), awaiting Volluk's next test of the Gauntlight. A hero who identified them knows they're starving: if the party fights them, throwing them a day's rations or fresh meat makes one spend its first turn eating.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: +2 circumstance to Recall Knowledge about scalathrax; thrown meat distracts them

key_abilities: Poorly fed: attacks on sight and pursues relentlessly

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Satchel Grown into the Wall
OPPORTUNITY.description: Pale fungus has grown thickly over a servant's satchel hanging from a wall hook, swallowing it whole. Only the strap and one buckle are still visible.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Cut it free without crushing what's inside: DC 19 Crafting or Thievery (10 minutes).
OPPORTUNITY.success: Inside are two Healing Potions (Lesser), their wax seals intact, and a note: 'The doors close by themselves now. I think the house is grieving.'
OPPORTUNITY.failure: One vial cracks as you cut. You save the other.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 4. Profusions of fungus grow everywhere on this level. Ephemeral spirits gently shut any door left open for more than a minute - the servant who wrote this didn't understand what they were.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Two Healing Potions (Lesser)

OPPORTUNITY.title: The Polite Dead
OPPORTUNITY.description: Behind you, the door you just came through swings gently shut on its own. A moment later, the one ahead of you does too. Nothing hostile - just a soft click, like a careful servant tidying up.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 19 Occultism or Religion to understand the spirits, and to ask them - politely - for help.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You realize the spirits close any door left open for more than a minute. You ask them to close doors behind you as you go, erasing your trail. Gain 1 Prepared token.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The doors keep closing, and you can't work out why. It's unsettling, but harmless.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 4. A canon feature of Belcorra's Retreat. Pursuers - including the cairn wights that hunt intruders across the level - lose the party's trail more easily. Prepared token: next time the party would add dice to the jar, add 1 fewer (minimum 0).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 1 Prepared token on a success

OPPORTUNITY.title: Coins from a Shuttered Mint
OPPORTUNITY.description: A gladiators' bench lies on its side, its rotten padding split open. A few old silver coins have worked their way out of the stuffing - thick, crudely struck, with a crowned lighthouse on one face.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 20 Society to recognize them.
OPPORTUNITY.success: These are from a mint that closed centuries ago. Collectors pay 4 gp apiece. You dig six out of the padding.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Old silver. You take them at face value (6 sp).
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 5. Canon: the waiting room (E15) sofa cushions hold 13 such coins - but that room is infested with fungal rot spores. This bench was dragged out into a corridor by something and is safe to search.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Six collector's coins (24 gp)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Vial in Assassin's Code
OPPORTUNITY.description: A small, thick-walled vial lies wedged in a crack, stoppered with black wax. Its label is a row of tiny symbols in a cipher, and a single drop of something oily has dried on the glass.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 20 Crafting to identify the contents, or DC 20 Society to crack the cipher.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Malyass root paste - a paralytic poison - labeled in the private code of an assassin. You also realize the assassin may still be here in some form.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Some kind of poison. You don't dare use it without knowing what it is.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 5. Seora Phade was Belcorra's chief assassin. She murdered two guards to escape after Belcorra's death, was mortally wounded, and now haunts the security checkpoint (E7) as a greater shadow. Her poison codex in E8 holds formulas for hunting spider venom, giant scorpion venom, giant wasp venom and malyass root paste.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Malyass Root Paste (identified on a success)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Fallen Victory Plaque
OPPORTUNITY.description: A tarnished silver plaque lies face-down in a corridor, dragged far from wherever it hung. Its rim is gouged with claw marks. On its face: 'CHAMPION VRASK - FORTY-ONE VICTORIES - 4239 AR.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 20 Athletics to straighten the bent mounting pins and carry it off without snapping it, or just take it as scrap.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The plaque survives intact (30 gp to a collector).
OPPORTUNITY.failure: It snaps; scrap silver only (10 gp).
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 5. The plaques in the Gladiators' Mead Hall (E25) commemorate victories between 4235 and 4244 AR - the only decade the arena operated, from the Gauntlight's completion to Belcorra's death. Grothluts dragged this one out, attracted to the shine.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Silver victory plaque (30 gp)

OPPORTUNITY.title: The Seugathi's Tally of Blades
OPPORTUNITY.description: A parchment has slid under a door: column after column of ticks and arrows in a careful, inhuman hand, each row labeled with a date. Someone has been recording the exact order of something - over and over - for weeks.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Study it: DC 20 Arcana or Crafting (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR).
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a record of a shuffling-scythe trap, kept by seugathi trying to find a pattern in it. There is no pattern - the blades really are random. Whoever built it must have left a passphrase.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Endless ticks. You give up before making sense of it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 5. Jafaki's minions stage attempts to disable the shuffling scythe blades (E20, a level-8 trap) from the staging area (E21). Only Chafkhem, the mummified arena administrator in E17, knows the passphrase. He's delighted to see the seugathi failing, and the parchment makes him one step friendlier.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Learn the scythe trap can only be safely disarmed with a passphrase; the parchment improves Chafkhem's attitude by one step

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Grothlut's Lab Tag
OPPORTUNITY.description: A dead grothlut lies in a puddle of its own fluids, a thing of mismatched limbs and too many mouths. A brass disc is riveted to what used to be its shoulder, stamped with alien script. A gold tooth glints in one of the mouths.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 20 Society or Occultism to read the seugathi script on the tag.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The tag reads (roughly): 'Morlock base. Batch 9. Reject - discard to the arena.' Holding it, you could pass yourself off as a handler returning a specimen.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Alien writing. The gold tooth is still worth 5 gp.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 5. Jafaki and the seugathi use this level as a dumping ground for failed experiments; grothluts are failed fleshwarps made mostly from morlocks. Graulgust on Level 2 rescued one from a cage down here.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Gold tooth (5 gp); lab tag gives +2 circumstance to one Deception check against seugathi on Floor 6

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Smuggler's Crate Marked C.R.
OPPORTUNITY.description: Stacked against a cave-in is a waterproofed crate stenciled with two letters: C.R. Inside: wrapped bottles, silver candlesticks, and a ledger page charred around the edges. The page is stamped DAWNFLOWER LIBRARY.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 20 Society to understand what the ledger page means.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The page is from Otari's Dawnflower Library - which was recently set on fire. The goods are stolen, and C.R. is Carman Rajani.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Stolen goods, by the look of it. You don't know whose.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 5. Carman Rajani recently burned a library and stole a historical relic (the Cooperative Blade) in a ploy to win political office, then hid in Smuggler's Refuge, which connects to this level through a cave-in behind the security checkpoint (E7). Captain Longsaddle pays a 30 gp bounty for evidence like this. How the party handles Carman matters on Level 7.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Two bottles of Elven Absinthe and 30 gp in candlesticks; evidence against Carman Rajani

OPPORTUNITY.title: An Ever-Burning Torch on the Ledge
OPPORTUNITY.description: Twenty feet down a dark shaft, a torch is wedged against a ledge, burning steadily. It gives off no heat and no smoke - and by the dust caked on it, it's been burning for centuries.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Climb down and back: DC 20 Athletics (10 minutes).
OPPORTUNITY.success: You retrieve an ever-burning torch that has fallen from the arena balcony above.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You slip halfway and fall to the ledge: 2d6 bludgeoning damage. You still get the torch, but the climb back up costs another 10 minutes.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 5. The six torches lighting the arena from the balcony (E26) are all ever-burning torches. Anyone exploring that balcony risks drawing the attention of the two basilisks in the Grand Concourse (E10).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Ever-burning torch (15 gp value)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Game of Towers
OPPORTUNITY.description: Two off-duty morlocks squat in an alcove over an upturned crate, slapping down grease-stained cards. A small pile of coins and a gold tooth sit between them. One looks up, sees you, and - instead of attacking - shoves a stool your way with a foot. 'Towers. You play?'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Sit in for a hand: DC 22 Deception to cheat, DC 22 Society or relevant Games Lore to play honestly, or DC 22 Diplomacy to just chat.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You win the pot (15 gp and a gold tooth worth 5 gp). The winner's mood loosens tongues: one of them is waiting to be called by the seugathi to become a drider, and can't stop talking about it.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You lose 10 gp and the morlocks laugh you off. No harm done.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 6. Morlocks waiting at the Warped Brew Tavern (F11) play a card game called Towers. Every few days Jafaki summons one from the tavern with the promise of being fleshwarped into a drider. It's a ruse: Jafaki dissects them for living parts for a flesh golem in the main laboratory (F25).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 20 gp pot; learn how Jafaki lures morlocks to his lab

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Devil's Dropped Report
OPPORTUNITY.description: A slip of reddish vellum lies on the floor, folded into a precise triangle and sealed with a dab of black wax pressed with a tiny pentagram. It smells faintly of sulfur.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 22 Society to read the Infernal inside, or DC 22 Thievery to lift the seal without breaking it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: A zebub's report to its master: 'Seugathi count holding at four. Jafaki never leaves the main laboratory. Stair guard unchanged.' With the seal intact, you could pass as a courier.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You break the seal reading it. The report is still useful, but the seal is ruined.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 6. Urevian sent a barbazu and two zebubs to establish a foothold in the torture chamber (F24); one zebub patrols invisibly. The seugathi ignore the devils' spies. Jafaki won't leave the lab to respond to intruders and trusts others to handle them.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Intel on the seugathi; an intact seal gives +2 circumstance to Deception against devils on Level 7

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Hellforged Dagger in a Corpse
OPPORTUNITY.description: A morlock corpse lies twisted against the wall, bearing all the marks of a slow, deliberate death. A dagger is still buried in its ribs - black steel with a faint heat shimmer, its pommel shaped like a horned skull.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 22 Religion or Crafting to understand the blade.
OPPORTUNITY.success: A hellforged dagger, made in a forge in Hell's style on the level below. You also recall how such a forge is destroyed: holy water.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A nasty dagger. You don't know where it came from.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 6. Urevian's devils torture seugathi minions they catch and dump the bodies. Hellforged weapons gain agile and deadly d8 in a devil's hands. The hellforge is in G5 on Level 7; splashing holy water on it cracks it with a 4d6 sonic + 4d6 evil blast (DC 23 basic Fortitude) - a hero who made this check knows that.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Hellforged dagger (worth a normal dagger, but menacing - most merchants refuse it); lore about the hellforge

OPPORTUNITY.title: Notes on Subject Meran
OPPORTUNITY.description: A chalk slate is propped against a wall, scrawled with alien glyphs and a sketch of a tall, muscular humanoid with a sigil on its forehead. One line is underlined three times.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 22 Society or Occultism to read the seugathi notes.
OPPORTUNITY.success: 'Subject Meran: exceptional fleshwarp candidate. Continue the arena victories and the gifts. Do not let the subject leave. Do not inform the subject.'
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Alien scribbles around a drawing of a brawler.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 6. Meran, a rare skulk brawler, lounges in the sauna (F22) with 'Victor' sigiled on his forehead, believing the seugathi will improve him and let him go home to chase championships. If shown this slate, he flees the Vaults instead of fighting and leaves his stash under the bench: a gold-and-emerald ring (40 gp), a ruby-encrusted dagger (70 gp) and a fine bracelet (20 gp).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Show Meran the slate and he stops fighting you - and offers you his stash

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Runaway Cask of Fungus Beer
OPPORTUNITY.description: A small cask has rolled into a corner, sloshing. It's branded with a crude mug and a tentacle. When you nudge it, the smell of sour, yeasty fungus fills the corridor.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Roll it back to the tavern: DC 22 Diplomacy when you deliver it. Or drink it: DC 22 Fortitude or sickened 1 for an hour.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The tavern's urdefhan manager is surprised anyone bothered. Her patrons start Indifferent toward you instead of Unfriendly.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: She takes the cask but doesn't warm to you. Patrons are still Unfriendly.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 6. Vischari, an urdefhan, murdered the Warped Brew's (F11) previous owner and made herself indispensable to the seugathi as manager. She attacks uninvited surface dwellers who threaten her livelihood, but she's a businesswoman first.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Warped Brew patrons start Indifferent instead of Unfriendly; or sell the cask for 10 gp

OPPORTUNITY.title: Shadow Malice's Set List
OPPORTUNITY.description: A crumpled sheet of fungus-paper lies under a bench, covered in scrawled song titles - 'Flesh Is Just a Phase', 'Jafaki Can't Have My Hands', 'Drider Lullaby' - with a 10 gp coin folded inside as a tip.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 22 Performance to learn the songs well enough to sing them back.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You know their material. If you ever face Shadow Malice in a battle of the bands, the crowd loves it.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Catchy titles. You can't make the tunes stick.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 6. Shadow Malice (Gulzash, Kragala, Nox and Ryta) are the Warped Brew's resident band. If the party shows interest, the morlocks start chanting the band's name and Ryta proposes a performance battle (DC 22 per round). Winning earns 80 XP, Vischari's respect, and on a critical success the band's instruments.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 10 gp; +2 circumstance to Phase 1 checks in the Battle of the Bands on a success

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Sketch of the Man in Colored Rags
OPPORTUNITY.description: Wedged in a drain grate is a scrap of cloth, charcoal smeared across it in a desperate, childlike hand: a tall figure in patchwork rags, holding a severed hand up like a prize. Beneath it, scratched over and over: HE TAKES IT. HE TAKES IT.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 22 Perception or Occultism to connect it to anything you've seen before.
OPPORTUNITY.success: If the party has met Dorianna Menhemes, you realize her 'motley man' and this figure are the same - and that whoever drew this lost a hand to him.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A disturbing drawing. You don't know who drew it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 6. Drawn by Jedzeli, a skulk prisoner in the Warped Brew kitchen (F12) whose right hand is missing. Before the denizen of Leng Ysondkhelir (G18) fixed on Dorianna, he tormented Jedzeli's dreams. Restoring Jedzeli's sanity is beyond the scope of the adventure, but her drawing points straight at the danger to the mayor's daughter.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: A clue to the Dorianna Menhemes subplot; +2 circumstance to checks to identify Ysondkhelir's influence

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Vial of Hydra Blood
OPPORTUNITY.description: A heavy glass vial with a brass screw-cap lies cracked but unbroken in a puddle, dark green blood clinging to the inside. A paper label in alien script is half washed away.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 22 Crafting or Nature to identify the blood and salvage it before it leaks out.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Hydra blood, prized for alchemy, magic and fleshwarping. You seal the crack with wax.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: It leaks away through the crack before you can seal it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 6. Belcorra kept a pair of hydras in her underground nature preserve (F4) for their blood; Jafaki keeps their descendants in a chemical stupor for the same reason. Each takes 3d4 rounds to wake fully if disturbed.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Vial of hydra blood (60 gp to an alchemist)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Page from Szek's Notebook
OPPORTUNITY.description: A torn page of cheap paper lies in a corner, covered in tiny charcoal handwriting in three languages. Most of it is a list of prisoners with notes like 'ground-shaper - good for knocking down bridges'. At the bottom, underlined twice: 'Still proud of locking that bossy wizard in with pitons. Hee!'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 23 Society to read the Infernal and Undercommon portions.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a page from the imp Szek's log of prisoners for the Otari invasion - and it's a signed confession that Szek locked Chafkhem in his room.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Scribbles and a list of names. You keep it anyway.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 7. Szek logs each stasis prisoner with recommendations for the Otari invasion (G9). Chafkhem, the mummified administrator in E17, rewards proof that Szek orchestrated his imprisonment with a full map of the Arena level (every secret door), the passphrase for the E20 scythe trap, and the spellbook page holding freedom of movement.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Proof for Chafkhem (Level 5) that Szek imprisoned him; returning it makes Szek Friendly at once

OPPORTUNITY.title: An Inventory for Burning Otari
OPPORTUNITY.description: A crisp sheet of parchment, ruled with fussy precision, is pinned under a rock as if it blew away mid-count. 'Barrels, pitch: 40. Jugs, lantern oil: 112. Fuse cord: 300 ft. Arrows: 2,400. Isolation cell: explosive arrow (1), spell-strike arrows (3), dragon's breath (3), alchemist's fire (10). Recount Tuesday. Recount Wednesday.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 23 Society to understand what it's for and where the items are stored.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's the supply list for a devil army's assault on Otari, kept by a meticulous zebub - including what's locked in the isolation cell of the storage block.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A long list of supplies. You don't know what it's for.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 7. The zebub Azvalviganer itemizes the equipment Urevian intends to use against Otari in the storage cells (G4), checking the inventory twice and then again. She holds the key to the locked isolation cell (G4a) and one of the five fragments of Urevian's pendant.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 30 gp bounty from Captain Longsaddle for proof of the planned attack; you know what's in the storage block's locked cell

OPPORTUNITY.title: An Imp's Cheat Sheet
OPPORTUNITY.description: A scrap of parchment tucked behind a door hinge has a single line of Infernal written on it, with the pronunciation spelled out phonetically underneath in Common, and a note: 'say it when you open the door, stupid.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 23 Religion or Society to understand what it does.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's the incantation that keeps doors here from flaring with fire when opened. Now anyone can say it - not just heroes trained in Religion.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Gibberish. You can't tell what it's for.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 7. Canon: every door on the prison level flickers with fire around its edges when opened or closed, which makes sneaking hard. Normally only a hero trained in Religion can suppress it with a brief incantation. Prepared token: next time the party would add dice to the jar, add 1 fewer (minimum 0).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Every hero can open doors on Floor 7 without them flaring; 1 Prepared token

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Scout's Report on Otari
OPPORTUNITY.description: A zebub has been squashed flat against the wall, as if something swatted it. Clutched in its legs is a rolled report. It describes Otari's streets, its garrison - and the heroes, by name, with notes on how they fight.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 23 Society to read the Infernal and work out who it was meant for.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The report was going to Ysondkhelir, who is making a detailed map of Otari. One line mentions 'the mayor's girl, who dreams of a motley man.' The devils know your tactics - which means you can change them.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: An unsettling report about you. You can't tell who was going to read it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 7. Urevian has been spying on Carman Rajani, so his forces know about the party; canon advises having devils call heroes by name or predict their tactics. Ysondkhelir convinced Urevian to have zebubs scout the surface and report to him, and used their reports to build his Otari map (G18).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: +2 circumstance to initiative in the next devil encounter; a clue to the Dorianna subplot

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Box of Strange Candle Stubs
OPPORTUNITY.description: A small wooden box lies spilled in the hall: candle stubs of dark, oily wax that smells of nothing on Golarion. Some are melted into shapes like curled fingers.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 23 Occultism to identify the wax and what it was used for.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Rare waxes used in dream rituals - someone here is reaching into a sleeping mind, night after night. The stubs are still valuable.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Expensive-looking candles. You don't know what they're for.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 7. Ysondkhelir performs dream rituals in G20 to invade and twist Dorianna Menhemes's dreams; a box of candles there is worth 50 gp. Slaying him frees Dorianna, and destroying his giant crawling hand restores her hand.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Rare wax candle stubs (20 gp); knowledge of the dream rituals targeting Dorianna

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Fallen Erinys Feather
OPPORTUNITY.description: A single black feather as long as your arm lies on the floor, its tips still glowing like embers. It's warm to the touch.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 23 Religion to understand what it's good for.
OPPORTUNITY.success: An erinys feather, saturated with infernal energy. Held during a ritual, it helps a mortal imitate the unholy power of a devil.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A big, hot feather. Worth something to an alchemist.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 7. Urevian's door (G10) needs all five fragments of his pendant - but a clever user can open it with four and a DC 25 Religion check to mimic the missing fragment's unholy energy. Failure deals 4d12 fire damage and stupefied 1 for an hour. The erinys smith Barkumuk (G5) and the twin erinyes in G7 shed these.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Erinys feather (60 gp to an alchemist), or +2 circumstance to the DC 25 Religion check to open Urevian's door with only four pendant fragments

OPPORTUNITY.title: Ingots on the Floor
OPPORTUNITY.description: A dropped sack has burst against the stone, spilling dull gray chunks of metal and two bright silver ones. Drag marks show a porter in a hurry - and a scorch mark where something with hooves stood.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 23 Crafting to identify the metals.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Cold iron and silver, stockpiled for weapons a devil smith hasn't forged yet.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Lumps of metal. Heavy ones.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 7. The erinys Barkumuk runs the hellforge (G5) and stacks unforged special metals beside his anvil - including an adamantine chunk worth 500 gp. He's openly grateful if the fussy zebub Azvalviganer is dead, but attacks anyway.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: 3 cold iron chunks and 2 silver chunks (10 gp each, 50 gp total)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Lost Dark Chase Piece
OPPORTUNITY.description: A small carved figure of polished jet lies in the mud of the path - a hooded runner with a tiny lantern, clearly a game piece. Its base is worn from centuries of hands sliding it across a board.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 24 Society to recognize the game and what this piece means to the people who play it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's from Dark Chase, a deep gnome board game. Some of the undead gnomes here have played the same incomplete game for decades - and its incompleteness is the point: with pieces missing, it can never end.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A pretty game piece. Worth a few gold.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. Three Children of Belcorra in the game room (H19) gamble endlessly on an incomplete Dark Chase set; they focus their rage on anyone who damages the game. Threatening to put this piece on the board - which could finally end the game - gives +4 circumstance to Intimidation or Diplomacy against them. Kalinth Narrogblom (Level 9) would love it too.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Jet game piece (10 gp); leverage over the Dark Chase gamblers

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Name-Stone for a Child of Belcorra
OPPORTUNITY.description: Half sunk in the muddy shore is a smooth, flat stone set with a polished blue gem. Tiny deep-gnome runes are carved around the gem: 'QUIET. Named by the Mistress. Year of the second harvest.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 24 Society to read the runes and understand what the stone is.
OPPORTUNITY.success: When Belcorra enthralled the deep gnomes here, she named them herself - and they treasured the names. This one belonged to a gnome called Quiet, now one of the bog mummies.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A pretty stone with writing on it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. The Children of Belcorra immured each other in the muddy shores to rise as bog mummies, waiting for her return. If the party meets a group of Children, one of them is Quiet (GM's choice): showing the stone makes that mummy stop fighting and try to take it back gently.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Star sapphire chip (120 gp); a Child of Belcorra shown its own name-stone stands down

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Chuul Egg Clutch
OPPORTUNITY.description: Fifteen feet down in the murky shallows, wedged in a nook of rock, you can make out a cluster of brown-and-purple eggs, each the size of a human head.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Dive for them: DC 24 Athletics to swim down, and DC 24 Stealth to do it without drawing the chuul that laid them (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR).
OPPORTUNITY.success: You surface with three intact chuul eggs.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A chuul notices the disturbance and comes for you. You can still grab one egg as you flee.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. The Cult of Urthagul ritually cooks and eats chuul eggs; the eggs in H3 are their last store. Custodian Dulac makes the party formal allies if they bring more eggs and clear the wisps around the cult's territory: they can rest in the shrine, and she grants safe passage through Galudu's lodge on Level 9.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Three chuul eggs: the key to Dulac's alliance with the caligni cult

OPPORTUNITY.title: Tribute for the Lazy Naga
OPPORTUNITY.description: A skiff has drifted against the shore, empty but for a heavy sack. Inside are ten pearls and a scrap of fungus-paper with a list in Undercommon: 'For the Overseer. More pillows. More pearls. Clean her rugs.' Someone has added at the bottom, in a different hand: 'Clean them yourself.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 24 Perception to spot the skiff in the mist; DC 24 Society to read the list.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You claim the pearls. The undead gnomes who were supposed to deliver them clearly resent their overseer.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The mist hides the skiff. You hear it bump against the rocks somewhere nearby, but never find it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. Belcorra put Vthis, a lazy, corrupt spirit naga, in charge of the Children (H25). The Children are loyal to Belcorra but resent Vthis, alternating between grudging obedience and ignoring her. The bulk of Vthis's hoard is in her secret treasury (H26).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Ten saltwater pearls (9 gp each, 90 gp)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Drow Message Cylinder
OPPORTUNITY.description: A slim bone tube lies in a patch of glowing moss, carved with elegant spider motifs and capped with wax. Inside, a message in Elven: 'The goliath spider took Velis and Draxx at the crossroads. Requesting aid from home. - N.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 24 Society to recognize the sender and destination.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's from Nyzuros, leader of the Yldaris drow scouting this level, to their home outpost below. Delivering it - or bringing it to Nyzuros - would earn real trust.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: A drow message. You can read it but don't know who sent it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. Nyzuros and four drow wardens (H45) are debating whether to fight the goliath spider at the crossroads (H35), which has eaten two scouts, or call for help from Yldaris. If the party kills the spider and lets Nyzuros take credit, he becomes Friendly automatically. Negotiating entry into Yldaris is worth 80 XP.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: +4 circumstance to Diplomacy with the Yldaris drow when delivered

OPPORTUNITY.title: Padli's Mushroom Wine
OPPORTUNITY.description: A full stoneware jug sits on a ledge, stoppered and sealed with wax pressed with a caligni sigil. It sloshes richly. Someone has scratched a little heart on the side.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 24 Society or Diplomacy to work out who would trade anything for it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: Mushroom wine - the favorite of Padli, the caligni cult's hedonistic second-in-command. He'd give a lot for it.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Strong-smelling wine. You keep it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. Padli (H6) favors mushroom wine and is as devout as Dulac, despite his hedonism. The secret door in the Hazy Shrine (H3, DC 25 Perception) leads down to Galudu's lodge on Level 9. The caligni know about it but are reluctant to reveal it.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Trade the jug to Padli to learn the hidden door between the cult's shrine and the lodge below

OPPORTUNITY.title: Glowing Reeds over Dark Water
OPPORTUNITY.description: A stand of reeds grows from a stone basin of brackish water, each stem glowing a soft green. The water in the basin is too still, and it smells like a swamp very far away.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Harvest some reeds: DC 24 Nature. DC 24 Occultism to understand the basin.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You cut a bundle of reeds that will glow for weeks without flame. And you realize the basin connects to a swamp far below - and that something uses these basins to watch.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The reeds wilt as you cut them. You don't know what the basin is.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 8. Belcorra's wisps hover over basins of brackish swamp water magically linked to the swamp on the temple level (J15), and use them to report intruders straight to her. Any wisp that sees the party in Chapters 8-9 triggers 'Belcorra Attacks!'. Bioluminescent reeds glow for weeks after harvest (H4).
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Glowing reeds (flameless light for 2 weeks); warning that the basins are Belcorra's eyes

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Whittled Figure That Looks Like You
OPPORTUNITY.description: On a flat rock beside the path sits a small figure carved from pale fungus-wood. It's one of you - unmistakably, down to your gear and the way you stand. Fresh shavings lie around it. Someone has been watching you, closely.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 26 Survival to follow the shavings and tracks back to the carver, or DC 26 Society to guess who made it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The trail leads to a drow guard who whittles while on duty. She's delighted you found it, and shows you the secret knock that gets visitors through the outpost door without a fight.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: The trail goes cold. You keep the figure.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. Rikizlia, a surly drow hunter, guards the passage up to the farm level (I1), whittling fungus wood on a stool. The Yldaris entry door (I5) has no handle and opens to a secret knock all outpost drow know; the warden Taklitur admits anyone who gives it. A wrong knock eventually earns crossbow bolts through the slot.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: The Yldaris secret knock; the guard becomes Friendly

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Marked Harrow Card
OPPORTUNITY.description: A single playing card lies face-down on a ledge. When you turn it over, it's a Harrow card with unsettling drow imagery - and its edges are notched with tiny, almost invisible scratches.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 26 Perception or Thievery to notice the marks and what they mean.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The deck it came from is marked. Whoever plays with it cheats - and now you know the marks.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Just a strange card.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. The shootist Yrorix and two hunters play cards with a drow Harrow deck in the watch chamber (I6) and cheat relentlessly. If the party are Yldaris's allies they're invited to play; a party who knows the marks wins the 24 sp in wagers and becomes popular. The well-worn deck itself is worth 15 gp.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Beat the drow at cards (24 sp) and earn their respect; +1 circumstance to Deception when gambling

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Fallen Bale from the Caravan
OPPORTUNITY.description: A heavy bale wrapped in oiled lizard hide lies in the fungus, its straps snapped. It smells of strange spices. A drow merchant's tally is stitched to the wrapping.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Carry it back to its owners: DC 26 Diplomacy when you return it. Or just open it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The caravan drow are surprised and grateful - surface people returning lost goods. They treat you as friends of Yldaris.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: They take the bale with a curt nod. No harm done, but no warmth either.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. Caravans between Yldaris and the drow city of Lozardyn load and unload in the caravan staging area (I2). Allied Yldaris traders sell any common item up to level 7 and can fetch others from Lozardyn in about a week.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Drow caravan goodwill (Friendly), or 30 gp in spices and cloth if you keep it

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Torn Page on Fulcrum Lattices
OPPORTUNITY.description: A page of heavy vellum is snagged on a thorny fungus, as if it fell from an armful of books carried past in a hurry. Diagrams of a lantern-like frame and four crystal lenses cover it, annotated in Aklo.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 26 Arcana or Occultism to understand the diagrams.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It describes a framework - a lattice - built to hold four lenses at the top of a lighthouse, and warns that bringing all four together draws something vast and hungry.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Complex diagrams. You keep the page but can't follow them.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. The grave knight Caliddo Haruvex fetched Belcorra's books from the Temple of the Canker (C34) and locked them in the Vault of Secrets (I58), dropping this page on the way. I58 holds her journals on the four fulcrum lenses, the lattice itself, and the skull-shaped key to the Gate of Nhimbaloth.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: +2 circumstance to Recall Knowledge about the fulcrum lenses and lattice; the vellum is worth 50 gp

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Cathlaj's Larder
OPPORTUNITY.description: On a high ledge, something has wedged a pile of corpses into a crevice - a cave lizard, two blind fish the size of dogs, and an urdefhan warrior, still armed. Long claw marks score the rock.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Climb up and loot the urdefhan: DC 26 Athletics (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR).
OPPORTUNITY.success: You recover the urdefhan's kukri, a fine weapon with a cruel edge. You're back down before whatever stocked the larder returns.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You're halfway up when you hear wings. You get down in time, empty-handed.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. A cathlaj recently nested on the Island Nest (I41) to lay eggs and stockpile corpses for its hatchlings. In the random-encounter table it returns to its nest after 2 rounds. The cathlaj eggs are worth 400 gp through Worliwynn's contacts near Otari.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: +1 striking kukri

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Runaway Riding Lizard
OPPORTUNITY.description: A huge lizard with a drow saddle still strapped to its back is licking moisture off a crystal growth. Its reins are torn. It eyes you warily but doesn't flee.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Calm it and lead it home: DC 26 Nature.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It lets you take the reins. Returning it to the drow earns real gratitude.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: It hisses and bolts into the fungus.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. The Yldaris drow keep half a dozen giant riding lizards in their stable (I3) and let young ones run free in the Lizard Run (I30), where they're aggressive toward non-drow humanoids since urdefhan killed two siblings. An escaped riding lizard is entry 1 on the Cavern Vast random-encounter table.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Yldaris traders sell to the party at a 10% discount

OPPORTUNITY.title: Runes Scratched by a Deep Gnome
OPPORTUNITY.description: Tiny, precise runes are scratched into the rock at knee height: 'Seeking my kin who came here long ago. If you find this, I went west. - K.N.' Beyond them, the scuffs of a struggle and a smear of blood.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 26 Society to read the deep gnome runes; DC 26 Survival to follow the signs of the struggle.
OPPORTUNITY.success: The trail leads toward the urdefhan war camp. Whoever K.N. is, they were taken alive.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You can't make out the runes, and the trail is lost on bare rock.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 9. Kalinth Narrogblom, a deep gnome rock warden, came looking for an offshoot of his people (he never met the Children of Belcorra). Urdefhan raiders captured him and keep him in a metal box in the summoning cavern (I35) to sacrifice. If shown evidence of the Children and led to an exit, he sends the Dark Chase set a week later.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Lead to Kalinth Narrogblom, whose rescue earns a jet-and-opal Dark Chase set (120 gp)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Mourner's Offering
OPPORTUNITY.description: In a niche carved with a moss-filled skull lies a small bundle wrapped in rotted black cloth. Inside are four gold rings, a lock of a child's hair, and a strip of reed paper: 'Bring her back to me as a ghost, and I will serve you forever.'
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 27 Religion to understand what the old worshipers believed, or simply take the rings.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You understand the offering: those who came here sought vengeance, an enemy's obliteration, or a promise that lost loved ones would return as ghosts. The rings are old and fine.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You take the rings without understanding what they were for.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 10. Long before Belcorra, the Gate of Nhimbaloth was a place of worship. Aspirants left offerings for the Lady's Whisper on its throne (I61), hoping it would rise and lead them to the initiation tests. The cult no longer exists.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Four gold mourning rings (150 gp total)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Spore Pod from a Dead World
OPPORTUNITY.description: A blackened pod the size of a fist sits in a crack in the black stone, still faintly pulsing. The swamp air around it is thicker and stranger than anywhere else.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 27 Nature or Occultism to understand what it is.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a seed of the poisonous swamp that echoes Nhimbaloth's dead world. Studying it, you learn how its toxins work - and how to breathe through them.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: An ugly seed pod. You don't recognize it.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 10. The Deadly Swamp (J15) echoes the poisonous terrain of Void Bracken, Nhimbaloth's dead world. Each creature starting its turn there must make a DC 27 Fortitude save or be sickened 2, and can't reduce sickened while in the swamp.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: +2 circumstance to saves against the toxic swamp air on this level; the pod is worth 100 gp to an occult collector

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Mote Escaped from the Vault
OPPORTUNITY.description: A tiny point of light and darkness drifts along the corridor, flickering between the two. It moves with purpose, as if it's going home.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Catch it in a container: DC 27 Reflex or Acrobatics. Then DC 27 Occultism to study it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a newborn wisp, not yet formed - and you realize where it came from: the place Belcorra waits is a pit that births wisps, linked to every swamp basin in the lower Vaults.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: It slips through your fingers and drifts away.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 10. The Empty Vault (J20) has always been a generation pit for Nhimbaloth's wisps. The soul feeders in J8 can only return to the Vault with more souls; if the party smashes the soul globes in J8, those wisps rejoin Belcorra in the final fight, making it much harder. A hero who studied the mote understands this before making that choice.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: A crucial warning about the final battle (see GM notes)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Cult Signet in the Muck
OPPORTUNITY.description: Something glints in the black swamp mud: a heavy signet ring carved as a tentacle wrapped around a skull, its mouth stuffed with moss.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: Dig it out of the toxic muck: DC 27 Perception (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR), and each hero helping must make a DC 27 Fortitude save against the swamp air.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You recover a signet of the old cult - the kind initiates wore after passing the tests.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: You find nothing, and the swamp air leaves you sickened 1.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 10. Initiates who passed the Challenge of the Swamp left gear behind in J15. The cultist specters in the Poisoning Room (J2) recognize the signet and hesitate for one round before attacking. Similar signets in Belcorra's vault (I58) are a ring of lies and a greater pendant of the occult.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Cult signet (100 gp); undead remnants of the cult hesitate for 1 round when it's shown

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Child at a Closing Door
OPPORTUNITY.description: The black stone ripples, and for a moment you're standing in a fine Absalom townhouse. A girl of six is being dragged from it by city guards, screaming, while her parents are marched out in chains. She looks straight at you with eyes full of hate. Then it's gone.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 27 Will save to watch without flinching. DC 27 Society to recognize the scene.
OPPORTUNITY.success: You hold steady. You understand: this is Belcorra's family being exiled from Absalom - the most traumatic day of her life, more than her death. Her rage is about this.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Frightened 1, and the vision leaves you shaken.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 10. The Empty Vault drew Belcorra's soul after the Roseguard killed her, and her ghost reappeared 500 years after her family's exile from Absalom for abhorrent rites - not after her death. When Nhimbaloth finally comes for her, she shrieks: 'My death is full of rage and strength - it is not empty!'
OPPORTUNITY.reward: +2 circumstance to one Intimidation or Deception check against Belcorra (taunting her about the exile)

OPPORTUNITY.title: A Shard of Green Glass
OPPORTUNITY.description: A jagged sliver of greenish glass lies on the floor, the size of a dagger blade. It glows faintly from within, and it's razor sharp.
OPPORTUNITY.challenge: DC 27 Crafting or Arcana to identify it.
OPPORTUNITY.success: It's a piece of a glass golem - one of the constructs that sliced up failed initiates after their souls were extracted. Something nearby broke it.
OPPORTUNITY.failure: Pretty green glass. You wrap it up carefully.
OPPORTUNITY.gm_notes: Floor 10. Glass golems in the Soul Extractors chamber (J7) cut apart failed initiates and carried their soul-filled crystal globes to the dread wisps in J8. Their greenish bodies give them 'grim glittering' instead of dazzling brilliance. A hero who identified the shard knows this before entering.
OPPORTUNITY.reward: Golem glass shard (80 gp); a warning about the glass golems nearby

COMPLICATION.title: Bored Bearded Devils on Patrol
COMPLICATION.description: Two bearded devils approach, their chains rattling. They're bored from centuries of guard duty and want entertainment. 'You! Surface-dweller! Prove you're worthy to walk Urevian's halls!'
COMPLICATION.challenge: DC 17 Performance to entertain (tell a story, sing, juggle) OR DC 18 Deception to claim you're 'expected guests of the contract devil'
COMPLICATION.success: They laugh and let you continue. One devil mentions 'avoid the Leng creature in the eastern cells - he steals hands.'
COMPLICATION.failure: They're offended or suspicious. 'Urevian will judge your worth in COMBAT!' Roll initiative.
