DILEMMA.title: Devil Trapped in Broken Summoning Circle
DILEMMA.description: A bearded devil is trapped in a malfunctioning summoning circle, chains sparking. 'Mortal! Free me and I'll owe you a favor! I know Urevian's contract secrets!'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Free them: they honor their word and whisper 'Urevian seeks Rajani souls' before vanishing. But you've made a devil ally...
DILEMMA.choice_b: Leave them: they curse you in Infernal. You avoid making deals with devils.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: If freed, reveals Urevian's goal (Carman Rajani's soul). Floor 7 specific. Devil may return as ally OR enemy later (GM choice).
DILEMMA.consequence: Moral vs tactical trade-off

DILEMMA.title: Urdefhan Warrior Trapped in Cave-In
DILEMMA.description: An urdefhan warrior is pinned under rocks, blood pooling. They rasp: 'Help... and I tell you... Khurfel's camp location... the Emerald Lens...'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Save them: free them. They honor their word, mark your map with Khurfel's war camp, then limp away. ADD 2 DICE TO JAR (20 minutes)
DILEMMA.choice_b: Leave them: they spit blood and curse you in Aklo. You miss crucial Floor 9 intelligence.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: If saved, reveals Khurfel's exact location and Emerald Lens info. Floor 9 specific. Urdefhan may remember this debt.
DILEMMA.consequence: Moral vs tactical trade-off

DILEMMA.title: Padli the Alcoholic Caligni Needs Help
DILEMMA.description: Padli, Dulac's selfish second-in-command, is drunk and lost. 'Help me back to... to the cult... Urthagul will be angry...' He's pathetic.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Show mercy: escort him back. He drunkenly reveals cult plans and Urthagul's location. ADD 2 DICE TO JAR (20 minutes)
DILEMMA.choice_b: Move on: let him find his own way. You preserve time.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 8 specific. Padli is alcoholic hedonist. If helped, reveals Cult of Urthagul plans and Crimson Lens location.
DILEMMA.consequence: Moral vs tactical trade-off

DILEMMA.title: Mitflit Negotiation - Talk or Fight
DILEMMA.description: A group of Mitflits block your path, chittering nervously. Their leader holds up a rusty spoon like a scepter. 'Sky King says... you give shinies! Or we stab-stab!'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Attempt negotiation: Give them shiny objects (coins, trinkets) to avoid combat and save resources, but takes time (ADD 1-2 DICE TO JAR). DC 16 Diplomacy.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Attack immediately: Surprise round against cowardly Mitflits, but use resources (HP, spells). They'll flee if 2+ die.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 1 specific. Mitflits worship rusty helmet as 'Sky King'. They want shiny objects (10-20gp worth satisfies them). If negotiation succeeds, they warn about Boss Skrawng's location. If attacked, they flee after 2+ casualties and alert Boss Skrawng.
DILEMMA.consequence: Diplomacy vs force trade-off

DILEMMA.title: Mitflit Ambush - Negotiate or Attack
DILEMMA.description: Mitflits pop out from hiding spots, shortbows drawn. 'Give shinies or we shoot-shoot!' They seem nervous and might flee.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Try to talk: Offer shiny objects (10gp worth), gain information about Boss Skrawng, but might fail and fight anyway. DC 16 Diplomacy.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Strike first: Surprise round and tactical advantage, but make noise that alerts other Mitflits nearby.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 1. Mitflits are cowardly - flee if 2+ die. Success reveals Boss Skrawng's giant maggot plan. Noise alerts 1d3 more Mitflits in 2 rounds.
DILEMMA.consequence: Combat or unfavorable deal

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Scouts - Negotiate or Attack
DILEMMA.description: Morlock scouts emerge from shadows, clubs ready. They grunt: 'Ghost Queen's domain! You pay or die!'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Try to talk: Offer rations/tribute, gain information about King Graulgust's forces, but might fail and fight anyway. DC 18 Diplomacy.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Strike first: Surprise round and tactical advantage, but make noise that echoes through tunnels.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2. Morlocks have darkvision 120ft and swarm tactics. Success reveals patrol routes or trap locations. Noise alerts King Graulgust if near his chamber.
DILEMMA.consequence: Combat or unfavorable deal

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Tribute - Talk or Fight
DILEMMA.description: Morlocks emerge from the darkness, grunting and gesturing. 'Ghost Queen... tribute... or blood!' They point at your supplies.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Attempt negotiation: Offer food/trinkets to avoid combat and save resources, but takes time (ADD 1-2 DICE TO JAR). DC 18 Diplomacy.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Attack immediately: Surprise round, but use resources (HP, spells). Morlocks swarm (+1 if 2+ adjacent).
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. Morlocks worship Belcorra as 'Ghost Queen'. They want rations or shiny objects. Success reveals King Graulgust's location or warns about traps. Track party reputation - if you've been generous before, DC drops to 16.
DILEMMA.consequence: Diplomacy vs force trade-off

DILEMMA.title: Ghoul Sentries - Negotiate or Attack
DILEMMA.description: Ghouls block the passage, claws extended. One hisses: 'Serve Canker... or become flesh for golem!'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Try to talk: Invoke Nhimbaloth or promise offerings, gain information about Nhakazarin, but might fail and fight anyway. DC 19 Religion or Diplomacy.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Strike first: Surprise round and tactical advantage, but risk paralysis if they counterattack. DC 15 Fort save.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3. Cult of Canker ghouls. Paralytic claws DC 15 Fort. Mentioning Nhimbaloth impresses them. Success reveals Temple of Canker location or warns about Aller Rosk.
DILEMMA.consequence: Combat or unfavorable deal

DILEMMA.title: Ghoul Parley - Talk or Fight
DILEMMA.description: Ghouls block your path, but they're not attacking yet. One speaks in broken Common: 'Flesh... for golem... or YOU become flesh!' They seem willing to bargain.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Attempt negotiation: Offer information about Nhimbaloth or promise to leave offerings, avoid combat (ADD 1-2 DICE TO JAR). DC 19 Diplomacy or Religion.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Attack immediately: Surprise round, but risk paralysis. Use resources (HP, spells). DC 15 Fort vs paralytic claws.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. Cult of Canker ghouls serve Nhakazarin. They seek 'cankerous flesh' for flesh golem in Temple (C34). Mentioning Nhimbaloth impresses them (DC drops to 16). Success reveals Nhakazarin's location or warns about Aller Rosk.
DILEMMA.consequence: Diplomacy vs force trade-off

DILEMMA.title: Urdefhan Patrol - Negotiate or Attack
DILEMMA.description: Urdefhan warriors step forward, weapons gleaming. 'Khurfel commands this level. State your business or face judgment!'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Try to talk: Show strength or offer tribute, gain information about Khurfel's forces, but might fail and fight anyway. DC 20 Intimidation or Diplomacy.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Strike first: Surprise round and tactical advantage, but they have Ferocity (don't fall at 0 HP) and will fight harder.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 9. Urdefhan respect strength. Wicked Bite deals 1d8 + 1d4 evil. Success reveals Emerald Fulcrum Lens location or drow alliance details.
DILEMMA.consequence: Combat or unfavorable deal

DILEMMA.title: Urdefhan Honor Duel - Talk or Fight
DILEMMA.description: Urdefhan warriors step forward, weapons ready. Their leader speaks: 'You trespass in Khurfel's domain. Fight with honor, or die like cowards!'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Attempt negotiation: Challenge to single combat or offer tribute to avoid full combat (ADD 1-2 DICE TO JAR). DC 20 Diplomacy or Intimidation.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Attack immediately: Surprise round, but face Ferocity (they don't fall at 0 HP). Use resources. Wicked Bite deals 1d8 + 1d4 evil damage.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 9 specific. Urdefhan serve Khurfel (holds Emerald Fulcrum Lens). They respect strength and honor. Single combat option: 1v1 duel to first blood, winner's party passes safely. Success reveals Khurfel's location or warns about drow alliance.
DILEMMA.consequence: Diplomacy vs force trade-off

DILEMMA.title: Mitflit Alarm System: Disarm or Rush
DILEMMA.description: Crude bells and cans block the passage. You could carefully disarm them or just rush through and deal with the noise.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Disarm carefully: 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 16 Thievery. Success = silent passage. Failure = alarm anyway.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Rush through: No time cost (NO DICE). Automatic alarm - all mitflits on floor alerted and hunting you.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Find alternate route: 20 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 17 Survival. Avoid this area entirely.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 1. Alarm brings 2d6 mitflits over next 10 minutes. Alternate route is safest but slowest.
DILEMMA.consequence: Time vs stealth - explicit dice cost

DILEMMA.title: Ghoul Scribes: Distract or Sneak
DILEMMA.description: Ghouls are copying texts, blocking your path. You could create a distraction, sneak past, or fight through.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Create distraction: 20 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR) to set up elaborate ruse. DC 17 Deception. Ghouls leave for 30 minutes.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Sneak past: 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). DC 18 Stealth. Success = pass unnoticed. Failure = combat.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Fight through: No time cost (NO DICE). Immediate combat with 1d4+1 ghouls. Loud and dangerous.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3. Distraction is safest but slowest. Sneaking is risky. Fighting alerts all ghouls on floor.
DILEMMA.consequence: Safety vs speed - dice jar tracks time

DILEMMA.title: Leech Pool: Wade or Detour
DILEMMA.description: A pool of leeches blocks the direct path. You could wade through (fast but dangerous) or find another way (slow but safe).
DILEMMA.choice_a: Wade through: 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). DC 17 Fortitude save. Failure = 2d6 bleed damage and drained 1.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Find detour: 25 minutes (ADD 3 DICE TO JAR). DC 16 Survival. Safe route around the pool.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Drain the pool: 40 minutes (ADD 4 DICE TO JAR). DC 18 Crafting. Pool is permanently drained - safe for future trips.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 4. Drained condition is serious. Detour is safe. Draining pool helps future exploration but costs lots of time.
DILEMMA.consequence: Risk vs time investment

DILEMMA.title: Gladiator's Ghost: Honor Duel or Refuse
DILEMMA.description: A gladiator's ghost challenges your strongest fighter to honorable single combat for a prize.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Accept duel: 20 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR) for full combat. Win = +1 striking weapon. Lose = ghost spares you but no prize.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Refuse honorably: 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR) to explain. DC 18 Diplomacy. Success = ghost respects you, gives lesser prize (50gp).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Refuse dishonorably: No time cost (NO DICE). Ghost and all arena spirits become hostile. Cursed: -1 to attacks for 24 hours.
DILEMMA.time_cost: 20 min vs 5 min vs 0 min + curse
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 5. Ghost fights fairly at party level. Honor matters. Dishonor brings wrath of all arena spirits (2d6 ghosts attack).
DILEMMA.consequence: Honor and reward vs time

DILEMMA.title: Seugathi Research Notes: Study or Destroy
DILEMMA.description: Detailed fleshwarp research notes. Studying them gives tactical advantage but takes time and might corrupt you.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Study thoroughly: 35 minutes (ADD 4 DICE TO JAR). Learn all fleshwarp weaknesses (+2 vs fleshwarps). DC 18 Will save or nightmares (-1 Will saves for 24 hours).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Skim quickly: 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). Learn one weakness. No corruption risk.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Destroy notes: 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). Seugathi lose research. No knowledge gained but you prevent future experiments.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 6. Full knowledge is powerful but corrupting. Destroying notes is heroic - seugathi can't create more fleshwarps.
DILEMMA.consequence: Power vs corruption vs heroism

DILEMMA.title: Devil's Contract: Negotiate or Refuse
DILEMMA.description: A bound devil offers a contract: power now, one favor later. The contract is binding but you can negotiate terms.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Negotiate carefully: 30 minutes (ADD 3 DICE TO JAR). DC 21 Diplomacy. Get +1 item now, owe reasonable favor later.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Sign quickly: 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). Get +1 item now, but favor is devil's choice (could be dangerous).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Refuse: No time cost (NO DICE). No deal. Devil remains bound. No power, no obligation.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 7. Devils ALWAYS keep contracts. Negotiated favor is one task (not suicide). Quick sign = devil chooses favor (dangerous).
DILEMMA.consequence: Power with obligation - time to negotiate matters

DILEMMA.title: Burial Mounds: Loot or Respect
DILEMMA.description: Ancient burial mounds contain treasure but disturbing them is desecration. You could loot them, perform rites, or leave them.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Loot respectfully: 25 minutes (ADD 3 DICE TO JAR). DC 17 Religion for proper rites. Gain 150gp + magic item. No curse.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Quick loot: 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). Gain 100gp. Cursed: -1 to all saves until you atone (requires remove curse).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Don't loot: No time cost (NO DICE). Perform rites only. Gain blessing: +1 to saves vs undead for 24 hours. No treasure.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 8. Respectful looting is best of both worlds. Quick loot curse is serious. Blessing without treasure is honorable.
DILEMMA.consequence: Greed vs respect vs honor

DILEMMA.title: Bog Mummy Memories: Listen or Hurry
DILEMMA.description: A lucid bog mummy wants to share its tragic story before it loses coherence. Listening takes time but might provide valuable information.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Listen fully: 30 minutes (ADD 3 DICE TO JAR). Learn floor layout, hidden treasures, and gain mummy's blessing (+2 to Diplomacy with undead).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Listen briefly: 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). Learn floor layout only. Mummy is disappointed but shares basics.
DILEMMA.choice_c: No time: No time cost (NO DICE). Mummy becomes hostile - you rejected its final wish. Must fight or flee.
DILEMMA.time_cost: 30 min vs 10 min vs 0 min + combat
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 8. Full story is tragic and valuable. Brief listen is practical. Rejection is cruel - mummy attacks with +2 to rolls (rage).
DILEMMA.consequence: Compassion vs time

DILEMMA.title: Faction Alliance: Negotiate or Stay Neutral
DILEMMA.description: A faction leader offers alliance against rivals. Alliance provides aid but makes other factions hostile.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Full alliance: 40 minutes (ADD 4 DICE TO JAR) to negotiate terms. DC 19 Diplomacy. Faction aids you in 2 combats. Other factions become hostile.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Temporary truce: 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 17 Diplomacy. Faction won't attack you. No aid, but no new enemies.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Stay neutral: No time cost (NO DICE). No allies, no new enemies. Navigate carefully.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 9. Roll faction: 1-2 drow, 3-4 urdefhan, 5-6 caligni. Alliance makes 2 other factions hostile. Aid is 1d4+1 warriors per combat.
DILEMMA.consequence: Allies vs enemies - political choice

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Scavengers - Trade or Take
DILEMMA.description: Two morlocks crouch over a pile of salvaged gear, arguing in Undercommon. They spot you and freeze. One clutches a healing potion, the other a rusted but functional crowbar. They don't attack - they're waiting to see what you do.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Trade fairly: Offer rations or a trinket. They accept eagerly, hand over the potion and crowbar, and scurry off. Takes 10 minutes of negotiation (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). DC 16 Diplomacy.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Intimidate them: Scare them into dropping everything and fleeing. DC 18 Intimidation. Takes 1 action. If failed, they shriek and flee - alerting King Graulgust's pack (next encounter is +2 morlocks).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Let them go: Wave them off. No time cost (NO DICE). They remember your mercy - next morlock encounter on this floor, morlocks hesitate 1 round before attacking.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. Morlocks worship Belcorra as 'Ghost Queen'. These two are low-ranking scavengers, not warriors. Trading builds goodwill. Intimidation risks alerting Graulgust. Mercy has delayed tactical benefit.
DILEMMA.consequence: Resources now vs stealth vs future advantage

key_abilities: Swarming Stance: +1 attack if sharing space

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Shrine - Desecrate or Respect
DILEMMA.description: You find a crude morlock shrine to the 'Ghost Queen' - a pile of bones arranged around a cracked mirror, with offerings of dead rats and shiny stones. Faint necromantic energy pulses from it. Destroying it would weaken morlock morale, but the noise would echo.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Destroy the shrine: 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). DC 17 Religion to disrupt the necromantic link. All morlocks on this floor lose Swarming Stance bonus for 1 hour. But the destruction echoes - next encounter arrives 1 round sooner.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Study the shrine: 20 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 18 Arcana or Religion. Learn that Belcorra channels power through these shrines. Gain +2 to saves vs necromantic effects on this floor.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave it: No time cost (NO DICE). Shrine continues empowering morlocks. No risk.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. Morlocks built this after sensing Belcorra's return 2 years ago. The 'Ghost Queen' connection is real - Belcorra does channel minor power through these. Destroying it is tactically smart but loud. Studying reveals lore about Belcorra's ghost nature.
DILEMMA.consequence: Weaken enemies vs gain knowledge vs avoid risk

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Prisoner - Free or Ignore
DILEMMA.description: A morlock is chained to the wall, beaten and starving. It whimpers when it sees you. Scratched into the wall beside it: 'TRAITOR TO GHOST QUEEN.' This morlock tried to leave Graulgust's pack.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Free the morlock: DC 16 Thievery to pick the manacles (5 minutes, ADD 1 DIE). The morlock is grateful - it knows a safe route that steers clear of Graulgust's throne room. Guides you safely, then flees.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Interrogate first, then free: 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 17 Diplomacy. Learn Graulgust's patrol patterns AND his safe route. Morlock also reveals a hidden cache of 50gp worth of salvage.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave it: No time cost (NO DICE). The morlock's cries might attract attention - 25% chance next encounter on this floor includes +1 morlock investigating the noise.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. This morlock, Grikk, defied Graulgust by hoarding food. Graulgust made an example of him. If freed, Grikk is genuinely helpful - he hates Graulgust. His safe route bypasses 1 encounter. Leaving him creates guilt AND potential noise problem.
DILEMMA.consequence: Quick help vs deep intel vs risk of noise
DILEMMA.creatures: 1 Morlock (Level 2, HP 38, AC 17 - currently at 12 HP, unarmed)

key_abilities: Swarming Stance: +1 attack if sharing space

DILEMMA.title: Graulgust's Offering Bowl - Poison or Bless
DILEMMA.description: A stone bowl sits at a junction, filled with rotting meat - offerings to King Graulgust from his subjects. Morlocks pass by regularly to add to it. You could poison it, bless it to weaken the undead energy, or use it as bait.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Poison the offerings: DC 17 Crafting or Nature. Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). When Graulgust eats, he becomes sickened 2 for 1 hour. Weakens the boss encounter significantly.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Bless the bowl: DC 18 Religion. Takes 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). Disrupts the necromantic 'Ghost Queen' connection. All morlocks on this floor lose their fanatical morale - they flee at half HP instead of fighting to the death.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Use as bait: Set an ambush here. Takes 20 minutes waiting (ADD 2 DICE). Next morlock to arrive can be captured for interrogation or eliminated quietly.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. Graulgust demands tribute from all morlocks. The bowl is checked every hour. Poisoning directly weakens the boss. Blessing breaks the Ghost Queen hold - morlocks become cowardly again. Ambush gives intel but costs the most time.
DILEMMA.consequence: Weaken boss vs break morale vs gain intel

DILEMMA.title: Undead Servant's Plea - Obey or Defy
DILEMMA.description: An undead servant blocks a doorway, still following 500-year-old orders. It rasps: 'None may pass without the mistress's seal.' It's not hostile - just following protocol. You could try to convince it Belcorra sent you, force past it, or find another way.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Bluff your way through: DC 18 Deception. 'Belcorra sent us to inspect the lower chambers.' Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). If successful, the servant steps aside and even offers directions. If failed, it attacks.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Destroy it: Combat with 1 Zombie Brute (Level 2, HP 50, AC 15). Takes 2-3 rounds. No dice added, but noise may attract 1d3 morlocks in 5 minutes.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Find another route: 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 16 Perception to find a side passage. Avoids the servant entirely but costs time.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. This servant died during Belcorra's reign and was raised as undead. It genuinely believes it's still serving. Mentioning 'Ghost Queen' confuses it (that's the morlock name, not Belcorra's). Using Belcorra's actual name works better. The side passage exists but is tight (squeeze rules).
DILEMMA.consequence: Social vs combat vs exploration

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Feast - Join or Disrupt
DILEMMA.description: You hear grunting and chewing ahead. A group of morlocks feast on a giant cave beetle, completely absorbed in their meal. They haven't noticed you. The passage you need goes right through their feast hall.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Sneak through during the feast: DC 17 Stealth (group check). Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). Morlocks are distracted - DC is lower than normal. If anyone fails, the morlocks attack mid-meal (they fight with -1 to attacks for 2 rounds, greasy hands).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Wait for them to finish and leave: 30 minutes (ADD 3 DICE TO JAR). Guaranteed safe passage. No risk, but significant time cost.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Create a distraction elsewhere: DC 16 Crafting or Thievery to rig a noise. Takes 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). Morlocks investigate the noise, clearing the path for 15 minutes.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. 1d4+2 morlocks feasting. They're genuinely distracted - Stealth DC is 2 lower than normal. If combat starts, morlocks are flat-footed for round 1 (still eating). The distraction option is clever and moderate cost. Waiting is safe but very expensive.
DILEMMA.consequence: Risk stealth vs waste time vs moderate effort

key_abilities: Swarming Stance: +1 attack if sharing space

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Sentry - Bribe or Ambush
DILEMMA.description: A lone morlock sentry guards a narrow passage, clutching a crude horn. If it blows the horn, every morlock on this floor will know you're here. It eyes you warily but hasn't raised the alarm yet.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Bribe with food: DC 15 Diplomacy. Offer rations. The morlock is hungry - Graulgust takes the best food. It accepts and 'looks the other way' for 10 minutes. Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Silent takedown: DC 19 Stealth + DC 17 Athletics. Rush and grapple before it can blow the horn. If Stealth fails, it blows the horn - all morlock encounters on this floor gain +1 morlock. If Athletics fails, it escapes and blows the horn while running.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Retreat and find another path: 20 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). Guaranteed safe. The sentry never knows you were here.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. The horn alert is SERIOUS - it adds +1 morlock to every remaining encounter on this floor. The bribe is cheap and effective. Silent takedown is high-risk high-reward. Retreating is safe but costly. Morlock sentries rotate every 2 hours.
DILEMMA.consequence: Cheap bribe vs risky silence vs expensive safety

key_abilities: Swarming Stance: +1 attack if sharing space

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Graffiti - Decode or Ignore
DILEMMA.description: Fresh morlock scratches cover the walls here - crude drawings of a crowned figure (Graulgust), a ghostly woman (Belcorra), and what looks like a map with X marks. This is morlock intelligence, scratched in their own pictographic language.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Decode the pictographs: 20 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 17 Society or DC 19 Survival. Learn locations of 3 morlock caches on this floor (50gp total) AND Graulgust's throne room location. Invaluable tactical intel.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Quick sketch and move on: 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE TO JAR). DC 15 Society. Copy the drawings to study later. Gain partial intel - learn Graulgust's throne room location only.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Ignore it: No time cost (NO DICE). It's just morlock scratches. You press on without the intel.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. Morlocks are smarter than they look - Graulgust has organized them with a crude communication system. The X marks are real caches where morlocks stash stolen goods. The throne room location lets players plan their approach to the boss. Quick sketch is the practical compromise.
DILEMMA.consequence: Full intel vs partial intel vs nothing

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Ambush Site - Spring It or Set Your Own
DILEMMA.description: You spot a morlock ambush ahead - crude tripwires, loose stones positioned to fall, and hiding spots behind pillars. The morlocks haven't arrived yet to man it. You got here first.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Disarm and pass through: DC 17 Thievery. Takes 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). Safe passage. When morlocks arrive to man the ambush, they find it dismantled and become confused (next morlock encounter on this floor, morlocks are flat-footed round 1).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Reverse the ambush: DC 19 Crafting. Takes 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE). Redirect the traps to face the OTHER direction. When morlocks arrive, their own trap triggers on them - 2d6 damage to 1d3 morlocks before combat even starts.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Hide and wait to ambush the ambushers: 20 minutes (ADD 2 DICE). When 1d3 morlocks arrive to man the ambush, YOU get the surprise round. But you're committed to combat.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. Graulgust has his morlocks setting ambushes throughout the floor. This one is unmanned - the morlocks rotate positions. Disarming is safe. Reversing is hilarious and effective. Waiting commits you to combat but with massive advantage. All three are good - it's about what resources you want to spend.
DILEMMA.consequence: Safe passage vs trap reversal vs guaranteed ambush

key_abilities: Swarming Stance: +1 attack if sharing space

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Wounded - Heal or Interrogate
DILEMMA.description: A morlock lies bleeding against the wall, badly wounded from a fight with something else - claw marks suggest ghouls from Floor 3 came up. It's dying. It looks at you with desperate, animal eyes.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Heal it: DC 15 Medicine. Takes 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). The morlock is shocked by your kindness. It tells you about the ghoul incursions from below - Floor 3 ghouls are raiding for 'cankerous flesh.' Warns you about Nhakazarin. Gives you a crude bone charm (+1 to Diplomacy with morlocks on this floor).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Interrogate before it dies: DC 16 Intimidation. Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). It gasps out that Graulgust is planning a 'great raid' on Floor 3 soon. If you time it right, you could let the morlocks and ghouls fight each other. Dies after talking.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Put it out of its misery: 1 action (NO DICE). Quick and merciful. No information gained. No moral weight on the party.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. The ghoul raids are real - Cult of the Canker sends ghouls up to grab morlocks for flesh golem parts. This morlock was a victim. Healing it gives lore about Floor 3 threats. Interrogation reveals the morlock-ghoul war timing. Mercy kill is the 'no info' option. The bone charm is a nice social tool for remaining morlock encounters.
DILEMMA.consequence: Compassion + lore vs intel about faction war vs nothing
DILEMMA.creatures: 1 Morlock (Level 2, HP 38, AC 17 - currently at 4 HP, dying)

key_abilities: Swarming Stance: +1 attack if sharing space

DILEMMA.title: Ghost Queen Mural - Deface or Preserve
DILEMMA.description: A large mural depicts Belcorra as the 'Ghost Queen' - painted by morlocks in crude but eerily accurate detail. She floats above kneeling morlocks, hands outstretched. The paint is fresh. Defacing it would be a powerful symbolic blow, but preserving it could teach you about Belcorra's ghost form.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Deface the mural: 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). No check needed. Morlock morale drops - next morlock encounter, they fight with -1 to attack rolls (shaken by the desecration). But Graulgust will be ENRAGED - his encounter gains +2 to attack rolls.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Study the mural: 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 18 Occultism or Religion. The mural is drawn from life - the morlocks have seen her. Gain +2 to Recall Knowledge about Belcorra for the rest of the campaign, and notice the faint seven-fingered handprint painted behind her: the mark of Nhimbaloth.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave it: No time cost (NO DICE). The mural stays. Morlocks remain inspired. No benefit, no risk.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. The morlocks have glimpsed Belcorra's ghost and painted her accurately. Defacing weakens the rank and file but enrages Graulgust, who never lets anyone say her name. The seven-fingered hand foreshadows the altar in D13 and the Empty Vault.
DILEMMA.consequence: Weaken troops but enrage boss vs gain lore vs nothing

DILEMMA.title: Morlock Pups - Protect or Use as Leverage
DILEMMA.description: You find a small alcove where morlock young huddle together, mewling. They're too small to fight. A morlock mother watches from the shadows, terrified but ready to die defending them. She holds a crude knife.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Show mercy and leave: 1 action (NO DICE). The mother morlock is stunned. She whispers a warning: 'Big ones... ahead... many.' You learn the next encounter has +2 extra morlocks than normal. She lets you pass safely.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Offer food and protection: DC 15 Diplomacy. Takes 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). The mother becomes an unlikely ally - she knows a safe path that bypasses the next 2 encounters entirely. She guides you, then returns to her pups.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Use them as leverage against Graulgust: DC 19 Intimidation. Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). Threaten to harm the pups unless Graulgust grants safe passage. If successful, Graulgust is FURIOUS but complies - you pass through his territory uncontested. If failed, every morlock on the floor attacks with +2 to damage (protective rage).
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2 specific. This is a MORAL dilemma with real tactical weight. Mercy gives intel. Kindness gives a guide. Leverage is powerful but risky and morally dark. Let the party debate - this reveals character. The mother morlock is named Skree. If helped, she appears in future Floor 2 visits as a friendly contact.
DILEMMA.consequence: Mercy + intel vs kindness + guide vs dark leverage
DILEMMA.creatures: 1 Morlock Mother (Level 2, HP 38, AC 17 - won't fight unless pups threatened)

key_abilities: Swarming Stance: +1 attack if sharing space
Protective rage: +2 damage if pups threatened

DILEMMA.title: Ghoul Scribe - Interrupt or Observe
DILEMMA.description: A ghoul sits at a desk, meticulously copying text from a crumbling tome into a fresh journal. It's so focused it hasn't noticed you. The book it's copying appears to be about Nhimbaloth rituals. The ghoul mutters: 'Must preserve... for the mistress...'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Observe and steal the copy: DC 18 Stealth. Wait 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE) for the ghoul to finish a section, then steal the journal when it goes to fetch another tome. Gain Nhimbaloth lore document (+2 to Occultism checks about Nhimbaloth for rest of campaign).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Interrupt and demand the book: The ghoul is startled but not immediately hostile - it's a librarian first, ghoul second. DC 17 Diplomacy to convince it you're 'researchers.' It lets you read the original tome for 20 minutes (ADD 2 DICE). Gain complete Nhimbaloth lore (+2 Occultism AND learn one weakness of Floor 10 enemies).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Kill it and take both books: Combat with 1 Ghoul (Level 1, HP 20, AC 16). Quick fight, but the noise alerts 1d3 more ghoul librarians who arrive in 3 rounds. You get both books but face reinforcements.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. Ghoul librarians are unique - they turned themselves into ghouls to keep serving Belcorra. They're scholars first. The Nhimbaloth lore is genuinely valuable for the endgame. Diplomacy works because these ghouls respect knowledge-seekers. Combat is fast but noisy.
DILEMMA.consequence: Partial lore quietly vs full lore socially vs loot with combat

DILEMMA.title: Augrael the Outcast - Ally or Avoid
DILEMMA.description: A ghoulish morlock sits alone in a reading nook, carefully turning pages of a history book. This is Augrael - rejected by both morlocks and ghouls. It looks up with intelligent, sad eyes. 'You're not here to eat me, are you? I just want to read.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Befriend Augrael: DC 14 Diplomacy (easy - he's desperate for company). Takes 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE). Augrael becomes a recurring ally. He knows every room on this floor, warns you about traps, and tells you Nhakazarin's daily routine. He asks only that you don't destroy the library.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Quick exchange: DC 15 Diplomacy. Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). Augrael tells you the safest path to the Scriptorium (C36) and warns about the web lurker nest. Less detail than full friendship but faster.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave him alone: No time cost (NO DICE). Augrael watches you go with disappointment. No benefit, but no risk either. He won't alert anyone - he has no loyalty to the Cult of the Canker.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. Augrael is a GREAT recurring NPC - a ghoulish morlock who survived the ghoul-morlock war but contracted ghoul fever. Rejected by both groups. Tranquil personality, only wants to read and eat undead flesh (not living). Treat like a biracial person with nowhere to belong. Befriending him is one of the best investments on this floor. He knows EVERYTHING about the library layout.
DILEMMA.consequence: Major ally investment vs quick intel vs nothing
DILEMMA.creatures: 1 Augrael (Ghoulish Morlock, Level 2, HP 30, AC 16 - non-hostile)

DILEMMA.title: Flesh Golem Parts - Destroy or Scatter
DILEMMA.description: You find a ghoul carrying a sack of 'cankerous flesh' - morlock body parts destined for the flesh golem in the Temple of the Canker (C34). The ghoul hasn't seen you yet. The sack is heavy and slowing it down.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Destroy the flesh: Kill the ghoul (1 Ghoul, Level 1, HP 20, AC 16) and burn the sack. DC 15 Survival to start a fire. Takes 10 minutes total (ADD 1 DIE). The flesh golem loses 10 HP permanently (parts can't be replaced easily). Smoke might attract attention.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Scatter the parts: DC 16 Stealth to sneak up, cut the sack, and scatter the flesh. The ghoul spends 30 minutes collecting it - one fewer ghoul in the next encounter on this floor. No combat, takes 2 actions.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Follow the ghoul: DC 17 Stealth. Takes 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE). The ghoul leads you directly to the Temple of the Canker (C34) - you learn the exact route and see the flesh golem's current state. Invaluable recon.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. The Cult of the Canker is stuck in an endless loop - they collect flesh for the golem but eat it themselves. This ghoul actually made it to delivery. Destroying the flesh directly weakens the golem. Scattering removes a ghoul from circulation. Following gives recon on the boss area. All three disrupt the cult's operation.
DILEMMA.consequence: Weaken golem vs remove enemy vs gain recon

DILEMMA.title: Ghoul Theological Debate - Intervene or Exploit
DILEMMA.description: Two ghoul librarians argue loudly about Nhimbaloth doctrine. One insists 'The Empty Death demands we PRESERVE knowledge!' The other snarls 'Knowledge is FLESH - we must CONSUME to understand!' They're about to come to blows. Neither has noticed you.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Side with the preserver: DC 17 Religion or Deception. Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). The 'preserver' ghoul is grateful and gives you access to a restricted section - gain 1 random scroll (GM picks appropriate level) and a map of this floor's trap locations.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Side with the consumer: DC 17 Intimidation or Deception. Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). The 'consumer' ghoul respects your ruthlessness and tells you where Nhakazarin keeps her personal stash - 75gp worth of gems hidden behind a loose stone in C34.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Let them fight: No time cost (NO DICE). Watch from hiding. They tear each other apart - one dies, the other is badly wounded (reduced to 5 HP). One fewer ghoul in future encounters. But the survivor is now hostile to ALL outsiders.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. The ghoul librarians have genuine theological disagreements about Nhimbaloth. This is darkly funny - undead scholars arguing about the nature of knowledge. Both sides offer real rewards. Letting them fight is the 'free' option but removes a potential ally. The preserver's map is very useful. The consumer's gem stash is nice loot.
DILEMMA.consequence: Scroll + map vs treasure location vs free enemy removal

DILEMMA.title: Zebub Spy - Capture or Bargain
DILEMMA.description: A zebub - a devil wasp the size of a cat - buzzes near the ceiling, watching you with compound eyes. It's a spy from Floor 7, recording everything it sees. It speaks in Infernal: 'Interesting... Urevian will want to know about you.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Capture it: DC 19 Athletics or Acrobatics to grab it. Takes 2 rounds. The zebub has recorded the last 10 minutes of your exploration - you can extract those memories (DC 16 Arcana) to see what IT has seen, including ghoul patrol routes and hidden doors. But capturing a devil's spy might anger Urevian on Floor 7.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Bargain with it: DC 17 Diplomacy or Deception. Takes 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). Offer information about the ghouls in exchange for information about Floor 7. The zebub tells you about Urevian's contract and the prison layout. Devils respect deals.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Kill it: Combat with 1 Zebub (Level 3, HP 30, AC 20). Quick fight but it has resistances (physical 5) and fire immunity. If killed, Urevian loses a spy - he won't know you're coming. But you gain no intel.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. Zebubs are devil wasps that record everything they see and can replay memories. This one reports to Urevian on Floor 7. Capturing gives you its recorded intel. Bargaining gives you Floor 7 preview. Killing removes Urevian's intelligence but gains you nothing. Devils respect contracts and deals - the bargain is genuine.
DILEMMA.consequence: Steal intel vs trade intel vs remove spy

DILEMMA.title: Ghoul Librarian's Request - Help or Refuse
DILEMMA.description: A ghoul librarian approaches you cautiously, hands raised. 'Wait - don't attack. I need help. A book has fallen into the web lurker nest and I can't retrieve it. It's 'Hymns of the Empty Shore' - Belcorra's annotated book of Nhimbaloth hymns. Help me get it and I'll let you read it.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Help retrieve the book: Enter the web lurker nest. DC 18 Stealth to avoid the lurkers, or fight 1 Web Lurker (Level 3, HP 45, AC 19). Takes 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE). Gain access to 'Hymns of the Empty Shore', annotated in Belcorra's hand. +2 to Recall Knowledge about Nhimbaloth for the rest of the campaign.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Demand the book as payment: DC 17 Intimidation. The ghoul agrees but is resentful - it retrieves the book itself (taking 30 minutes) and hands it over. You get the book (ADD 3 DICE for waiting) but the ghoul warns other ghouls about you (+1 ghoul in next encounter).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Refuse: No time cost (NO DICE). The ghoul shrugs and shuffles away. You miss the Nhimbaloth lore. The book remains in the web lurker nest.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. A lesser companion to The Whispering Reeds, which stays hidden in the Secure Collection (C35). The hymns' margin notes mention that 'the Reeds' are kept somewhere the scribes never go - a hint toward C35. Helping the ghoul is the best deal; demanding works but has social consequences.
DILEMMA.consequence: Risk for major lore vs time + social cost for lore vs nothing
DILEMMA.creatures: 1 Web Lurker (Level 3, HP 45, AC 19) if entering nest
DILEMMA.reward: +2 to Recall Knowledge about Nhimbaloth for the rest of the campaign

DILEMMA.title: Ghoul Feeding Frenzy - Intervene or Exploit
DILEMMA.description: You hear snarling ahead. Three ghouls have caught a morlock raider from Floor 2 and are fighting over the body. They're completely distracted by their feeding frenzy, clawing at each other as much as the corpse. 'Cankerous flesh! MINE!' 'For the golem!' 'I'm HUNGRY!'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Sneak past during the frenzy: DC 14 Stealth (group check - very easy, they're distracted). Takes 2 actions (NO DICE). Clean bypass. But the ghouls finish feeding and resume patrol in 10 minutes.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Attack while they're distracted: All 3 ghouls are flat-footed and prone (feeding). You get surprise round AND they start prone. Combat with 3 Ghouls (Level 1, HP 20, AC 16 each - AC 14 while prone). Eliminates a patrol permanently.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Throw food to lure them away: DC 15 Survival or Nature. Toss rations down a side corridor. Takes 1 action (NO DICE). Ghouls chase the food, clearing the path for 20 minutes. No combat, no risk, but uses 1 day's rations.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. The Cult of the Canker ghouls are supposed to collect flesh for the golem but they can't stop eating it themselves - this is their core dysfunction. The feeding frenzy is a perfect ambush opportunity. Sneaking is easy and free. Attacking removes a patrol. Luring with food is creative and costs only rations. All three are good options.
DILEMMA.consequence: Free bypass vs eliminate patrol vs creative distraction
DILEMMA.creatures: 3 Ghouls (Level 1, HP 20, AC 16 each - currently prone and flat-footed)

DILEMMA.title: Ghoul Courier - Intercept or Follow
DILEMMA.description: A ghoul rushes past carrying a sealed scroll tube, muttering 'Nhakazarin demands this immediately... the ritual cannot wait...' It's heading toward the Temple of the Canker (C34). The scroll might contain ritual instructions or intelligence.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Intercept the courier: DC 17 Athletics to tackle, or DC 18 Stealth to snatch the tube. Takes 1 round. The scroll contains Nhakazarin's ritual notes - learn that the flesh golem needs 3 more 'donations' before completion. Gain +2 to checks against the golem. But the ghoul escapes and alerts Nhakazarin that someone stole her notes.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Follow to the Temple: DC 17 Stealth. Takes 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE). The ghoul leads you to C34. You see the Temple layout, the golem's current state, and Nhakazarin's defenses. Complete recon of the boss area.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Let it pass: No time cost (NO DICE). The ritual progresses. The golem gets closer to completion. But you remain undetected.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3 specific. The courier is delivering ritual components to Nhakazarin. Intercepting gives mechanical advantage against the golem but alerts the boss. Following gives complete recon - arguably more valuable. Letting it pass maintains stealth but the golem gets stronger. The '3 more donations' detail is a timer - players could try to prevent those donations.
DILEMMA.consequence: Golem intel + alert boss vs full recon vs maintain stealth

DILEMMA.title: Wight Patrol - Parley or Ambush
DILEMMA.description: Two wights in ancient guard uniforms patrol a corridor. They still follow 500-year-old orders, marching in formation. One carries a rusted halberd, the other a cracked shield. They haven't seen you yet. Their patrol route passes a narrow chokepoint ahead.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Ambush at the chokepoint: Set up at the narrow passage. Takes 10 minutes waiting (ADD 1 DIE). When they arrive, you get surprise round AND they can only approach single-file. Tactical advantage. Combat with 2 Wights (Level 3, HP 50, AC 18). Drain Life: DC 17 Fort or drained 1.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Attempt to command them: DC 19 Deception. Impersonate Belcorra's authority: 'The mistress commands you to stand down.' Takes 1 action. If successful, they salute and march away - encounter avoided entirely. If failed, they attack immediately (no surprise for either side).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Wait for them to pass: 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). They patrol past your hiding spot. DC 15 Stealth (easy - they're predictable). Safe passage but time cost.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 4 specific. These wights are Belcorra's ancient guards - they still follow patrol routes from 500 years ago. They respond to authority because they were soldiers. The Deception check to impersonate Belcorra's authority is high but the payoff is huge. Ambushing at the chokepoint is tactically sound. Waiting is safe but expensive. Drain Life is dangerous - DC 17 Fort or drained 1.
DILEMMA.consequence: Tactical combat vs social bypass vs safe but slow

key_abilities: Drain Life: DC 17 Fort or drained 1
Wight Spawn: slain humanoids rise as wights in 1d4 rounds

DILEMMA.title: Voidglutton Warning Signs - Prepare or Flee
DILEMMA.description: The air grows cold. Reality flickers. A faint, hungry presence presses against your minds. DC 15 Occultism or Religion to recognize the signs: the Voidglutton is nearby. This Level 8 EXTREME creature is twice your level. It's the only entity on the upper floors that can communicate with Belcorra.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Prepare defenses: 15 minutes (ADD 2 DICE TO JAR). DC 18 Occultism. Set up protective wards. If the Voidglutton appears, party gets +2 to Will saves against its abilities for the first 3 rounds. Might be the difference between survival and TPK.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Retreat immediately: 10 minutes (ADD 1 DIE - moving quickly through explored territory). Fall back to a defensible position. The Voidglutton doesn't pursue beyond its territory. Safe but you lose progress and must re-approach later.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Press forward carefully: DC 19 Stealth (group check). No time cost (NO DICE). Try to pass through the Voidglutton's territory without attracting its attention. If failed, the Voidglutton appears - EXTREME encounter with no preparation.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 4 specific. The Voidglutton is a Level 8 EXTREME encounter - it can TPK the party. The AP doesn't stress this enough. It's the only entity on upper floors that communicates with Belcorra. Preparing defenses is the smart play if you plan to fight. Retreating is the safe play. Sneaking through is high-risk - failure means an unprepared EXTREME encounter. WARN PLAYERS about the danger level. This should feel terrifying.
DILEMMA.consequence: Prepare for EXTREME fight vs safe retreat vs gamble on stealth

DILEMMA.title: Ancient Guard Post - Recruit or Destroy
DILEMMA.description: Two wights stand at attention in an ancient guard post, staring straight ahead. They're in a dormant state - following their last order to 'guard this post until relieved.' They won't attack unless provoked or until someone tries to pass. A clever commander could potentially give them new orders.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Give new orders: DC 20 Deception. 'You are relieved. Report to the meditation pavilion for reassignment.' Takes 5 minutes (ADD 1 DIE). If successful, the wights march away - they guard the meditation pavilion instead, creating a safe fallback point with undead guards. If failed, they attack.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Destroy them while dormant: Surprise round with both wights flat-footed. Combat with 2 Wights (Level 3, HP 50, AC 18). They're easier to kill while dormant but it's still a resource expenditure. Permanently clears this guard post.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Sneak past: DC 16 Stealth (group check). No time cost (NO DICE). They remain dormant. But they'll activate if you retreat through here later - potentially trapping you between enemies.
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 4 specific. These wights are in a dormant state - a feature of Belcorra's ancient military. They follow orders from anyone who sounds authoritative enough. Redirecting them to guard the meditation pavilion is brilliant - it creates a safe rest point. Destroying them is straightforward. Sneaking past leaves a potential problem for retreat. The DC 20 Deception is high but the payoff is enormous.
DILEMMA.consequence: Recruit undead guards vs eliminate threat vs leave potential trap

key_abilities: Drain Life: DC 17 Fort or drained 1
Wight Spawn: slain humanoids rise as wights in 1d4 rounds

DILEMMA.title: Footlocker in the Collapsed Barracks
DILEMMA.description: Half buried under fallen roof timbers is an iron-banded footlocker stenciled with a faded lighthouse crest - the mark of Belcorra's household guard. Something inside sloshes when you tilt it.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Smash it open: DC 15 Athletics. NO DICE ADDED. It's loud - the next Floor 1 encounter cannot be surprised by the party - and the glass vial inside breaks. You get 3 gp and a dented guard's badge.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Pick the lock: DC 15 Thievery. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). Everything survives: 3 gp, the badge, an intact Healing Potion (Minor), and a folded duty note.
DILEMMA.consequence: Speed and noise vs. a careful search
DILEMMA.reward: Healing Potion (Minor), 3 gp, and a lore note (lockpicking only)
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 1. The duty note, in a guard's scrawl: 'The Mistress laughed at the rumors of Absalom spies. She says they will only ever see the top floor.' This matches the truth: the Roseguard never learned the Vaults existed below the keep. Badge: 1 gp to a collector.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave it. NO DICE ADDED. Nothing gained, nothing risked.

DILEMMA.title: Barrel of Fly Feed
DILEMMA.description: Someone has dragged a rotting barrel into a sheltered corner and filled it with dead fish, waterfowl and cat-sized beetles. Flies the size of your thumb crawl over it. Muddy mitflit footprints lead back and forth from it toward the maggot pens.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Spoil it: pour lamp oil or something foul in. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). Every Giant Maggot and Giant Fly on Floor 1 is sickened 1 for the rest of the day.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Use it as bait: drag it into a dead-end and wait. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). In the next Floor 1 combat that includes maggots or flies, they're distracted by the food and flat-footed in round 1.
DILEMMA.consequence: Weaken Skrawng's 'cavalry' now or set up an advantage later
DILEMMA.reward: A floor-wide weakening of Boss Skrawng's maggots and flies, or a round-1 advantage
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 1. This is the food supply for Skrawng's maggot-to-fly 'war steeds' (A4-A6). If the mitflits find their barrel ruined they blame each other and squabble for an hour.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Ignore it. NO DICE ADDED.

DILEMMA.title: A Message Scratched for Zarmavdian
DILEMMA.description: Low on a wall, half hidden by creepers, someone scratched letters into the stone with a knife point: 'Z - she is falling back toward the servants' lounge. Going around to cut her off. - O.' The cuts are old, the edges worn smooth.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Take a charcoal rubbing: DC 15 Crafting. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). Morlibint at Odd Stories or Mayor Oseph will pay for it.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Pry the whole stone out: DC 15 Athletics. ADD 2 DICE TO JAR (20 minutes, 4 Bulk). It sells for far more - but Mayor Oseph is upset if he learns you hacked up the town's founding site.
DILEMMA.consequence: Respect for history vs. profit
DILEMMA.reward: Rubbing: 15 gp. Stone: 40 gp (and the mayor's displeasure)
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 1. Written by Otari Ilvashi, the Roseguard rogue, to the wizard Zarmavdian during the 4244 assault. Otari did reach her: the fight ended in the servants' lounge (now the A8 sinkhole) when Belcorra's last-ditch explosion collapsed it and swallowed him. She fled to the lighthouse (A11), where the other Roseguard killed her. The rubbing is a strong conversation piece with Otari's ghost later, and it convinces Morlibint to look harder for Zarmavdian's spellbook connection.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave it where it is. NO DICE ADDED. You remember the words.

DILEMMA.title: A Message from the Captured Thieves
DILEMMA.description: Scratched into the plaster at knee height, with what looks like a belt buckle: 'GORU SHAD ZILLI ALIVE. MUSHROOM-EYES KEEP US BEHIND THE WORKSHOP. BRING FOOD.' Beneath it, a crude bird in flight.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Go now: head straight for the workshop. NO DICE ADDED. You arrive while the morlock engineers are mid-argument over a ballista - they're flat-footed in round 1.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Prepare first: gather rations and plan the approach. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). You arrive with food for the starving prisoners; they can walk out under their own power and won't slow the party down.
DILEMMA.consequence: Speed vs. readiness - or abandoning the prisoners
DILEMMA.reward: Yinyasmera's 50 gp reward for the thieves; flat-footed engineers or self-sufficient prisoners
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 2. The three surviving Osprey Club thieves are held in B24 behind timbers wedged against the door in B22 (removing them is a 3-round activity). Two Ghost Queen morlock engineers in B22 try to capture intruders alive to appease Graulgust. The thieves' gear is in B23.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Ignore it for now. NO DICE ADDED. Each day the party delays, roll a DC 11 flat check; on a failure another thief dies.

DILEMMA.title: The Cult's Discard Pile
DILEMMA.description: In an alcove is a heap of books the cult has thrown out - anything that isn't about Nhimbaloth, necromancy or Belcorra. Cookbooks, poetry, a bestiary, travel journals. The ghouls don't care about any of it. Morlibint would.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Grab an armful: NO DICE ADDED. You take 1 Bulk of books at random - roll a d6, and on a 5 or 6 one of them is a Morlibint title worth a 10 gp bonus.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Sort it properly: DC 18 Perception, ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). Success: 2 Bulk of books, including the Morlibint title. Critical success: 3 Bulk.
DILEMMA.consequence: Time vs. a better haul
DILEMMA.reward: 1-3 Bulk of books for Morlibint (5 gp per Bulk) plus a possible 10 gp bonus
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 3. Canon side quest: Morlibint pays 5 gp per Bulk; delivering 12 Bulk completes it. Each room in the library has a fixed number of Bulk (C11: 2, C33: 6, etc.); this discard pile is extra. A failed sort still yields 1 Bulk.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave it. NO DICE ADDED.

DILEMMA.title: The Scalathrax Feed Bucket
DILEMMA.description: A bucket of rotting meat sits outside a heavy door, abandoned halfway through a delivery. From behind the door comes a frantic scrabbling of many legs and a hungry clicking.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Poison the meat: DC 19 Crafting or Nature using anything toxic you carry. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). If the party later fights the scalathrax, they're sickened 2.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Take it as bait. NO DICE ADDED. In any later fight with the scalathrax, toss them the meat and one spends its first turn eating.
DILEMMA.consequence: Weaken the scalathrax in advance, or distract them later
DILEMMA.reward: Sickened 2 scalathrax, or one loses its first turn
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 4. Volluk keeps two scalathrax poorly fed in their pen (D10) for his next Gauntlight test; one was already teleported into Otari during the Deadtide. They attack on sight and pursue relentlessly.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave it. NO DICE ADDED.

key_abilities: Poorly fed: attacks on sight and pursues relentlessly

DILEMMA.title: A Fleeing Servant's Pack
DILEMMA.description: A small skeleton lies face down in a side passage, a knife in its back and a pack still strapped to its shoulders. It was running somewhere. Its outstretched hand points down a slippery tunnel.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Grab the pack and go. NO DICE ADDED. You get 6 gp and a stoppered vial - roll a d6, and on a 4 or higher it's an intact Healing Potion (Lesser).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Search it properly: DC 19 Perception, ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). You get the coins, the potion (intact), and a sketch map the servant drew of a way out.
DILEMMA.consequence: Speed vs. the full picture
DILEMMA.reward: 6 gp, a possible Healing Potion (Lesser), and the location of an escape route to the coast
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 4. One of the servants murdered by the chef on Belcorra's orders. The map shows the Twisting Tunnel (D15): slippery ledges out of the lake cavern (D14) to sea caves west of Otari - the route the werewolf Jaul Mezmin uses to come and go. The cave mouth is underwater even at low tide.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave it. NO DICE ADDED.

DILEMMA.title: A Ghost Lanista's Drill
DILEMMA.description: A translucent woman with a whistle and a scarred face steps out of the wall. 'You lot. You call that a stance? I've trained champions who killed manticores. Fall in.' She paces in front of you, waiting.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Drill with her: each hero attempts DC 20 Athletics or Acrobatics. ADD 2 DICE TO JAR (20 minutes). Every hero who succeeds gets +1 circumstance to attack rolls in their next combat on Floor 5.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Ask her about the arena instead: DC 20 Diplomacy. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). She tells you where the mimics nest and that the gladiators' plaques prove the arena only ran for ten years.
DILEMMA.consequence: Training vs. intel vs. time
DILEMMA.reward: +1 circumstance to attack in the next Floor 5 combat, or the mimics' location
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 5. Belcorra hoped to make this a premier gladiator facility to select officers for her army; the arena ran from 4235 to 4244 AR. The mimics are in the gladiator readiness room (E13), disguised as a weapon rack and a fallen door.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Refuse. NO DICE ADDED. She spits on the floor and fades.

DILEMMA.title: A Page from the Poison Codex
DILEMMA.description: A single brittle page has blown into a corner: a hand-inked formula with neat diagrams of a wasp's stinger and a list of reagents. The paper flakes at the edges as you look at it.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Copy it before it crumbles: DC 20 Crafting. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). You learn the formula for Giant Wasp Venom.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Sell it: Yinyasmera at Crook's Nook pays 40 gp for it intact. Carrying it safely takes a DC 20 Thievery check to seal it between boards. NO DICE ADDED.
DILEMMA.consequence: Knowledge vs. money vs. conscience
DILEMMA.reward: Giant Wasp Venom formula, or 40 gp
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 5. A page from Seora Phade's exceedingly fragile poison codex (E8). The first time anyone opens the codex they must succeed at a DC 20 Thievery check or a random formula disintegrates - this is one that did.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Burn it. NO DICE ADDED. One less poison in the world.

DILEMMA.title: A Mimic Wants a Lift
DILEMMA.description: A wooden chest sits in the middle of the corridor. As you approach, it clears its throat. 'Don't. Please. I'm not hungry for you - I'm just sick of this hall. Nothing tasty comes through anymore. Carry me somewhere better, and I'll tell you where the shiny is.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Carry it: ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes, 4 Bulk). Set it down somewhere busier and it tells you about a lead-lined box in the viewing room that holds a ring - and that only careful fingers open it.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Attack it while it's playing nice. NO DICE ADDED. It's flat-footed in round 1.
DILEMMA.consequence: Trust a monster vs. take the advantage
DILEMMA.reward: Directions to a type I ring of wizardry, or a surprise round
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 5. The dented lead-lined steel box in the Elite Viewing Room (E9) can't be forced, only opened with a DC 20 Thievery check, and holds a type I ring of wizardry bearing the symbol of Nhimbaloth. Two poltergeist siblings haunt that room; they vanish for good if the party describes a clear path of open doors to the surface.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Decline politely. NO DICE ADDED. It sighs and goes back to waiting.

DILEMMA.title: A Morlock on Her Way to Be Remade
DILEMMA.description: A morlock woman hurries down the hall, practically skipping, clutching a summons scrawled in alien glyphs. 'I've been called! Finally! Jafaki's going to make me a drider!' She notices you and beams. 'Are you here to be warped too?'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Warn her: DC 22 Diplomacy. NO DICE ADDED. She believes you and flees upward. But Jafaki will run out of morlocks sooner - and then start on the members of Shadow Malice.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Take her place: DC 22 Deception to borrow her summons and pass as the next subject. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR. When you knock on the lab door, Jafaki's drider opens it expecting a willing victim, and you get a surprise round against them.
DILEMMA.consequence: Save one life, endanger others - or use her
DILEMMA.reward: A surprise round against Jafaki and the drider, or a life saved
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 6. Canon: every few days Jafaki summons a morlock from the Warped Brew with the promise of becoming a drider, then dissects them for the flesh golem in F25. Jafaki always sends the drider to answer a knock, since other seugathi sometimes come for guidance - the party can exploit that habit.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Let her go. NO DICE ADDED. One more set of living parts goes on the flesh golem.

DILEMMA.title: The Devils Want the Stair
DILEMMA.description: A barbazu steps out of a side passage, glaive lowered but ready, beard writhing. 'Mortals. You're no friends of the worms, I'd wager. There's a seugathi guarding the great stair. Remove it, and my master will remember you kindly when you come below.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Accept and do it. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR. On Level 7, Urevian's devils treat you as contractors: +2 circumstance to Diplomacy with them, and the barbazu at the drill field holds off attacking for a round to hear you out.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Refuse. NO DICE ADDED. The barbazu shrugs and leaves. Nothing changes.
DILEMMA.consequence: Picking a side in the devil-seugathi truce
DILEMMA.reward: Goodwill with Urevian's devils on Level 7
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 6. Jafaki killed Belcorra's bone devil overseer Tarkannah, starting a months-long war with Urevian's devils that ended in an uneasy truce. A single seugathi and a chained grothlut guard the Central Shaft (F1). If the landing goes unguarded for 5 days, Urevian sends a barbazu and two driders to take it.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Accept, then double-cross: tell the seugathi. DC 22 Deception. NO DICE ADDED. The seugathi doesn't care, but the devils learn you lied - every devil on Level 7 starts hostile.

DILEMMA.title: Unlabeled Vials
DILEMMA.description: A collapsed shelf has scattered dozens of small vials across the floor - some cloudy, some glowing, some with things floating in them. None are labeled in any language you know.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Sort them properly: DC 22 Crafting. ADD 2 DICE TO JAR (20 minutes). You find 2 Healing Potions (Moderate) and an Antidote (Moderate), and safely leave the rest.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Grab a handful. NO DICE ADDED. Roll a d6 for each of three vials: 1-2 Healing Potion (Moderate), 3-4 inert, 5-6 a fleshwarping agent (DC 22 Fortitude or enfeebled 1 for a day if drunk).
DILEMMA.consequence: Time vs. gambling
DILEMMA.reward: Up to 2 Healing Potions (Moderate) and an Antidote (Moderate)
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 6. The seugathi store reagents carelessly; much of it is spoiled or experimental. A character who sorts carefully also recognizes the fleshwarping agents and can bottle one as evidence of the experiments (Morlibint pays 10 gp for it).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Leave them. NO DICE ADDED.

DILEMMA.title: The Prototype Head
DILEMMA.description: In a waste bucket full of tubing sits a morlock's head, its skin waxy, wires running from its neck into a dead battery of jars. Its eyes open and find you. Its lips move: 'Kill... me... I know how... the machine...'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Listen, then end it: DC 22 Medicine to keep it lucid long enough. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). It whispers exactly which tube to cut first in Jafaki's machine.
DILEMMA.choice_b: End it at once. NO DICE ADDED. A mercy, but it takes its secret with it.
DILEMMA.consequence: Mercy now vs. mercy with knowledge
DILEMMA.reward: +2 circumstance to the Occultism check to safely disconnect Jafaki's occult machinery
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 6. An earlier prototype of the living morlock head in Jafaki's main laboratory (F25). Disconnecting that machinery takes DC 22 Occultism. On a failure (or if it's smashed), the trapped energies animate another stitched body as a flesh golem - Belcorra's flesh statue in the Temple of the Canker (C34) if it was left intact - which hunts the party through the Vaults.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Walk away. NO DICE ADDED.

DILEMMA.title: A Letter for Carman Rajani
DILEMMA.description: A barbazu blocks the hall - not attacking, just holding out a sealed scroll tube between two clawed fingers. 'Mortals. You go up to Otari, yes? Deliver this to a man named Carman Rajani. Unopened. You'll be paid.' It tosses a heavy purse at your feet.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Take the job and deliver it unopened. NO DICE ADDED. 150 gp. Urevian's offer reaches Carman - who may bolt.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Open it first: DC 23 Thievery to unseal and reseal it undetectably. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). You learn what Urevian really wants before you meet him, and can still choose whether to deliver it.
DILEMMA.consequence: Money vs. knowledge vs. staying out of devil business
DILEMMA.reward: 150 gp, or advance knowledge of Urevian's offer (+2 circumstance to Diplomacy and Society checks when negotiating with him)
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 7. Urevian needs the soul of Carman Rajani, the last descendant of Vol Rajani, to repay a far more powerful devil - and his contract says only Belcorra, or one of her mortal foes, can deliver it. In exchange he'll leave the Material Plane with all his devils, which drops the barrier on the G3 elevator. If Carman is warned, the party may have to pay Urevian to scry him out later.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Refuse. NO DICE ADDED. The barbazu shrugs and flies off with its letter.

DILEMMA.title: Szek's Devil's Luck Contract
DILEMMA.description: A voice stammers from empty air at shoulder height: 'Close the door - close the door! Psst. Surface people. You're taking down Urevian, right? Bad business, keeping him around. How about a little contract? Devil's luck. Very fair terms. I'd make a wonderful servant for someone less... shouty.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Sign it. NO DICE ADDED. The signer gains devil's luck (once per day, reroll a failed check), and Szek serves them - but the contract binds the signer's soul to Hell.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Decline politely: DC 17 Diplomacy. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes of talking). Szek becomes Friendly anyway and tells you everything she knows: the five pendant fragments and who holds them, and that Urevian wants out of his deal with Belcorra.
DILEMMA.consequence: Power vs. your soul vs. intel
DILEMMA.reward: A daily reroll (at the cost of your soul), or the location of all five pendant fragments
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 7. Szek (G9) is tired of running errands for Urevian and hopes to sign a devil's luck contract. She stays invisible until made Friendly (DC 17 Diplomacy vs. her Will DC). Fragment holders: the slag gagon in F5, Azvalviganer (G4), Barkumuk (G5), the erinyes sisters (G7) and Ysondkhelir (G18). She also proudly admits locking Chafkhem in his room.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Threaten her. NO DICE ADDED. She vanishes, and every devil on the level hears about you within the hour.

DILEMMA.title: A Message Meant for a Sleeping Girl
DILEMMA.description: A zebub buzzes past at speed carrying a tiny scroll case, too intent to notice you. You could swat it out of the air.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Take the scroll and use it yourself: DC 23 Occultism. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). You send a warning into Dorianna Menhemes's dreams, giving her the strength to resist the motley man a little longer.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Take it and read where it was going: DC 23 Society. NO DICE ADDED. You learn where the motley man performs his rituals.
DILEMMA.consequence: Protect Dorianna now, or find her tormentor faster
DILEMMA.reward: Dorianna's decline slows by 2 days, or the location of Ysondkhelir's ritual room
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 7. The zebub carries a scroll of dream message from Ysondkhelir's hand collection (G19). He uses zebubs as messengers and dream rituals in G20 (charcoal drawings of Dorianna cover the walls). Slaying him frees Dorianna; destroying the giant crawling hand restores her hand.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Let it go. NO DICE ADDED.

DILEMMA.title: The Children Offer You a Name
DILEMMA.description: Four small figures caked in dried mud step onto the path and bow stiffly. The eldest speaks in a voice like wet gravel: 'You are strong. The Mistress gave us names when we were living. We would name you, and you would be one of her Children. Then you need not fear us.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Accept a name. NO DICE ADDED. Bog mummies on Floor 8 treat that hero as kin and won't attack unless attacked. But the name marks them: Belcorra and her wisps sense them more easily, a -2 circumstance penalty to Stealth against them on Floors 8-10.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Decline gracefully: DC 24 Diplomacy. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes of ceremony). They give you a lesser gift instead - a carved name-stone worth 50 gp - and let you pass.
DILEMMA.consequence: Safety now vs. Belcorra's attention later
DILEMMA.reward: Bog mummies won't attack the named hero, or a 50 gp name-stone
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 8. Belcorra named the deep gnomes she enthralled and called them her Children. After her death they chose undeath to keep their numbers up, waiting for her return.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Decline rudely. NO DICE ADDED. They take it as an insult to the Mistress. Roll initiative.

DILEMMA.title: A Caligni Scout Asks for Help
DILEMMA.description: A gaunt, shadowy figure steps out from behind a fungus stalk with both hands raised. 'Please. I serve the Custodian. The ghost queen's lights keep us from our god - we can't reach him. You could clear them. She would reward you.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Agree. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes to hear the plan). The scout guides you to Custodian Dulac, who starts Friendly instead of hostile and explains her offer.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Rob him. DC 24 Intimidation. NO DICE ADDED. You get his pouch (25 gp and a Cheetah's Elixir (Moderate)), but the whole cult turns hostile.
DILEMMA.consequence: An alliance vs. a quick profit
DILEMMA.reward: Dulac starts Friendly (cult alliance), or 25 gp and an elixir
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 8. Belcorra posted wisps (including two dread wisps in H10) to keep the caligni Cult of Urthagul away from the Crimson Fulcrum Lens, which the gug Urthagul holds in the Island Cavern. Dulac's deal: more chuul eggs and the fringe wisps gone, in exchange for rest in the shrine and safe passage through Galudu's lodge.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Decline. NO DICE ADDED. He slinks back into the dark.

DILEMMA.title: A Summons from the Overseer
DILEMMA.description: A bog mummy shuffles up and presents a mud-stained scroll, bowing. In elegant, lazy handwriting: 'Visitors are to present themselves - and a gift - to the Overseer at once. Do not dawdle. Do not be boring.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Bring her a gift of at least 50 gp in goods. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). Vthis is placated and tells the Children to leave you alone - they're happy to ignore you.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Ignore the summons. NO DICE ADDED. The messenger reports back. Vthis is too lazy to do anything about it herself, but sends her dread wraith to watch you.
DILEMMA.consequence: Bribe, ignore, or ambush
DILEMMA.reward: Free movement among the Children, or an ambush advantage against Vthis
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 8. Vthis, a scheming spirit naga (H25), lounges all day ordering the Children to bring food and treasure. She prefers black tentacles and paralyze in combat and surrenders below 40 HP. Her dread wraith lookout haunts the Shadowed Dock (H23).
DILEMMA.choice_c: Use it to get close and ambush her. NO DICE ADDED. Approaching on her invitation, you get +2 circumstance to initiative against her.

DILEMMA.title: The Master Warden's Offer
DILEMMA.description: A stern drow woman in polished armor steps out of the shadows, flanked by wardens. 'Surface dwellers. I am Salaisa Malthulas. You will bring trouble down on Yldaris whether you mean to or not.' She sets a heavy purse on a rock. 'Two hundred gold to go around our home and never come back.'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Take the money. NO DICE ADDED. 200 gp, but no Yldaris alliance - no meeting with Quara, no seers, no safe rest.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Win her over: DC 26 Diplomacy. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). She remains wary but becomes an ally of sorts, and Yldaris's doors open to you.
DILEMMA.consequence: Money vs. allies vs. drow politics
DILEMMA.reward: 200 gp, or the Yldaris alliance (rest, trade, the seers' lens lore)
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 9. Salaisa is master warden and second-in-command; she becomes leader if anything happens to Quara (I14). She's constantly on the move and can be met anywhere near Yldaris. She fears unknown surface dwellers will put the community at risk. Allying with Quara is worth 120 XP and reveals where the Ochre lens lies.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Report her to Quara later. NO DICE ADDED (for now). Quara trusts you more (+2 circumstance to Diplomacy with her), but Salaisa becomes a quiet enemy.

key_abilities: Loyal to Yldaris to the death

DILEMMA.title: Caligni Looking for a Way Out
DILEMMA.description: Two shadowy caligni defenders crouch behind a boulder, studying the cavern walls. They flinch when they see you. 'We seek a road out for our people. A daemon blocks one way, a dragon the other. Do you know another?'
DILEMMA.choice_a: Tell them about the bat passage, if you've found it. NO DICE ADDED. Their leader Galudu will pay you once her people are through.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Offer to escort them. ADD 2 DICE TO JAR (20 minutes). You meet Galudu, learn the full plan, and earn her trust - but urdefhan death scouts are waiting for the refugees to come into the open.
DILEMMA.consequence: Helping the refugees, and the risk that comes with it
DILEMMA.reward: Galudu's magic wand when her people escape
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 9. Galudu (I26), a caligni mage, feeds the lodge refugees with conjured food. She wants a safe exit: past the derghodaemon (I31), past Ravirex (I51), or through I42, which she doesn't know about. Escorting the caligni triggers a Severe urdefhan ambush, but the caligni fight alongside the party.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Send them away. NO DICE ADDED.

DILEMMA.title: The Shootist's Last Notes
DILEMMA.description: A drow shootist lies dead in a narrow passage, her body torn by something with far too many legs. Her repeating crossbow lies beside her, and a small leather journal is tucked inside her armor.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Grab the crossbow and go. NO DICE ADDED. A fine repeating hand crossbow (+1).
DILEMMA.choice_b: Read the journal properly: DC 26 Society. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR (10 minutes). Her last entries describe tracking where Larathol dropped the ochre lens during his last fight - near the island's east shore.
DILEMMA.consequence: Loot vs. knowledge vs. respect
DILEMMA.reward: +1 repeating hand crossbow; the Ochre lens's location; or Quara's deep gratitude
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 9. The gogiteth (I48-I49) kills anything in its territory. Quara's father Larathol and her older sister died on a secret expedition to the island, killed by Khurfel; he dropped the Ochre lens in the water to deny it to his enemy. Finding it takes detect magic or DC 28 Perception while searching off the east shore of I41 - a hero who read the journal gets +2 circumstance.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Take her body home to Yldaris. ADD 2 DICE TO JAR (20 minutes). The drow are moved: +4 circumstance to Diplomacy with Quara, and they return her crossbow to you as thanks.

DILEMMA.title: A Soul in a Crystal Globe
DILEMMA.description: A crystal sphere a foot across lies in a corner where something dropped it. Inside, a pale shape presses its hands against the glass, mouth moving silently. It's a person - or what's left of one.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Smash it. NO DICE ADDED. The soul goes free to the Boneyard. The hero who smashes it gets +2 status to a single check of their choice within the next month, even after seeing the result.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Keep it. NO DICE ADDED. Certain unsavory buyers - night hags, for instance - pay 200 gp for a trapped soul.
DILEMMA.consequence: Mercy vs. profit vs. an easier path now
DILEMMA.reward: A +2 status bonus, 200 gp, or one fewer soul feeder in the Devouring Chamber
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 10. Failed initiates had their souls extracted into crystal globes in J7; three globes remain there, each worth 200 gp to unsavory soul merchants. The soul feeders in J8 vanish one per globe smashed there - but they return to the Empty Vault and fight beside Belcorra. The status bonus mirrors Pharasma's reward for freeing Borbo's soul on Level 2.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Carry it to the soul feeders. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR. Smashing it in front of them satisfies one, and it vanishes from that room - straight to Belcorra's side in the final battle.

DILEMMA.title: Rest While She Recovers?
DILEMMA.description: You've found an empty, silent chamber - the first place in days where nothing is hunting you. Everyone is exhausted. But if you've already beaten Belcorra once, you know she's re-forming somewhere below, and every hour brings her closer to full strength.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Take a long rest. ADD 6 DICE TO JAR. Everyone recovers fully. Belcorra's rejuvenation advances by a day.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Take a short rest. ADD 1 DIE TO JAR. Recover Hit Points with Treat Wounds and refocus, but spent spell slots don't return.
DILEMMA.consequence: Your strength vs. hers
DILEMMA.reward: Full recovery, or catching Belcorra before she's ready
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 10. Canon: the party can rest as long as they need in this level's empty chambers. A defeated Belcorra rejuvenates in 2d4 days; the Ebon Fulcrum Lens on the Vault's altar hastens it, and it automatically rejuvenates her when the heroes arrive if she hasn't finished. Only infusing her with the Crimson, Emerald and Ochre lens splinters destroys her for good.
DILEMMA.choice_c: Press on now. NO DICE ADDED. You reach her before she's fully re-formed - if she hasn't finished, the Ebon lens finishes the job the moment you arrive, but she's still incensed and fights in fury.

DILEMMA.title: The Shrouded Guide Points East
DILEMMA.description: The skeletal figure in grave-cloth glides ahead of you and stops beside a gray stone door carved with swirling mist. It points at the door, then at you, then waits - patient as a tombstone.
DILEMMA.choice_a: Follow its lead. NO DICE ADDED. It opens the doors for you and the trials go in order - but each one you pass makes it angrier, and it will turn on you at the end.
DILEMMA.choice_b: Refuse and attack. NO DICE ADDED. It answers as if it expected this: it levitates out of reach and teleports heroes into chambers full of wisps and traps.
DILEMMA.consequence: Trust, defiance, or a long con
DILEMMA.reward: Ordered trials and open doors, or a prepared ambush when it betrays you
DILEMMA.gm_notes: Floor 10. The Lady's Whisper guides the party through the Challenge of Souls, Despair and the Swamp in that order only if they follow it; otherwise they may tackle them in any order.
